skills.description: Choose between mutexes, binary semaphores and counting semaphores to protect shared peripherals and signal events between tasks.

skills.name: Reproduce and fix priority inversion
skills.description: Reproduce priority inversion on target with three tasks and a shared mutex, then fix it with priority inheritance and confirm with traces.

skills.name: Compute in Q15 and Q31 fixed-point formats
skills.description: Multiply, add and scale Q15 and Q31 values with correct shifts, rounding and saturation, and convert between fixed-point and physical units.

skills.name: Implement a first-order low-pass filter in firmware
skills.description: Implement an exponential first-order low-pass filter, compute its coefficient from cutoff frequency and sample rate and verify the step response.

skills.name: Implement a discrete PID controller in firmware
skills.description: Code a discrete PID with output clamping, integrator anti-windup, derivative on measurement with filtering and bumpless mode changes.

skills.name: Implement cascaded position, velocity and current loops
skills.description: Implement nested position, velocity and current loops in firmware, tune inner to outer and enforce limits at each level.

skills.name: Close a current loop on a brushed DC motor
skills.description: Close a PI current loop around a brushed motor using synchronized current sensing, giving direct torque control with limits.

skills.name: Measure motor resistance, inductance and constants in firmware
skills.description: Measure winding resistance, inductance, torque constant and pole pairs with firmware test routines using voltage injection and spin tests.

skills.name: Apply Clarke and Park transforms
skills.description: Convert three-phase currents to stationary alpha-beta and rotating d-q frames and back, and verify the transforms numerically.

skills.name: Generate space vector PWM
skills.description: Compute space vector PWM duty cycles from an alpha-beta voltage command, including sector selection and overmodulation limiting.

skills.name: Compute electrical angle from encoder and pole pairs
skills.description: Compute rotor electrical angle from mechanical encoder position, pole-pair count and alignment offset, and wrap it correctly.

skills.name: Align the encoder to the rotor magnetic field
skills.description: Find the encoder electrical offset by driving a fixed d-axis voltage, confirm direction and pole pairs, and store the result.

skills.name: Tune d- and q-axis current PI loops
skills.description: Tune d and q current PI controllers from measured resistance and inductance for a target bandwidth, and test the step response.

skills.name: Field-oriented control firmware for a BLDC joint
skills.description: Combine current sensing, transforms, current PI loops, SVPWM and electrical angle into a working torque-controlled BLDC joint at kilohertz rates.

skills.name: Run FOC with SimpleFOC
skills.description: Set up SimpleFOC on a supported board and driver, configure sensor, motor and loop parameters and run torque, velocity and angle modes.

skills.name: Configure an ODrive or moteus controller
skills.description: Configure an ODrive or moteus controller with motor and encoder calibration, gains and limits, and command it over CAN or USB.

skills.name: Store configuration in flash or EEPROM
skills.description: Store calibration and configuration in flash or EEPROM with a version number, CRC and wear-aware writes, and fall back to safe defaults.

skills.name: Use watchdogs and fault states
skills.description: Configure independent and window watchdogs, feed them only when all critical tasks are healthy, and log the reset cause after recovery.

skills.name: Handle brown-out and reset causes
skills.description: Enable brown-out detection, read reset-cause flags at startup and choose safe behavior after power dips or unexpected resets.

skills.name: Implement a firmware fault state machine
skills.description: Implement latched fault states with clear conditions for overcurrent, overtemperature, encoder loss and communication loss, reporting fault codes to the host.

skills.name: Implement overcurrent, overvoltage and thermal limits
skills.description: Implement firmware current, bus voltage and temperature limits with derating and hardware comparator or break-input fast trips.

skills.name: Implement safe torque off in a joint controller
skills.description: Remove motor torque through gate-driver disable that does not rely on firmware, and verify behavior together with brakes and e-stop.

skills.name: Design a firmware bootloader
skills.description: Design a bootloader with separate flash regions, image header with version and CRC, vector table relocation and a safe jump to the application.

skills.name: Update firmware over CAN
skills.description: Transfer and flash a new image to a joint controller over CAN with chunked, acknowledged transfers and integrity checks before booting it.

skills.name: Version and identify firmware builds
skills.description: Embed version, git hash and build configuration in firmware images and report them over the bus so every joint's build is traceable.

skills.name: Set up a single-board computer running Linux
skills.description: Flash an OS image to a Raspberry Pi or similar board, configure networking, SSH, users and updates, and verify headless operation.

skills.name: Set up an NVIDIA Jetson with JetPack
skills.description: Install JetPack on a Jetson module, select power modes, verify CUDA and camera support and monitor thermals and memory.

skills.name: Control GPIO from Linux with libgpiod
skills.description: Read and write GPIO lines and wait for edge events from Linux using libgpiod tools and bindings rather than deprecated sysfs.

skills.name: Access serial devices from Linux
skills.description: Open serial devices with pyserial or termios, set baud and raw mode, and create udev rules for stable device names.

skills.name: Use CAN from Linux with SocketCAN
skills.description: Bring up a CAN interface with ip link, monitor traffic with candump and cansend, and read and write frames from Python or C sockets.

skills.name: Start robot software at boot with systemd
skills.description: Write systemd units that start robot processes at boot in the right order, restart on failure and log to the journal.

skills.name: Install and verify a PREEMPT_RT kernel
skills.description: Install or build a PREEMPT_RT kernel and measure scheduling latency with cyclictest under load to compare against a standard kernel.

skills.name: Configure real-time threads on Linux
skills.description: Run a control thread with SCHED_FIFO priority, locked memory, preallocated buffers and CPU isolation, and check its period jitter.

skills.name: Bridge a microcontroller to ROS 2 with micro-ROS
skills.description: Run micro-ROS on a microcontroller with an agent on the host to publish sensor topics and subscribe to commands over serial or UDP.

skills.name: Bridge joint controllers into ros2_control
skills.description: Write a ros2_control hardware interface that reads joint states from and writes commands to embedded controllers each control cycle.

skills.name: Bring up a new microcontroller board
skills.description: Bring up a new board stepwise: check rails and current, connect the debugger, blink a pin, verify clocks, then enable peripherals one at a time.

skills.name: Sequence robot power-on and actuator enable
skills.description: Define and implement a power-on sequence where logic, sensors and communication are verified before motor power and torque enable.

skills.name: Unit test firmware logic on the host
skills.description: Compile hardware-independent firmware modules for the host and test them with a unit test framework and mocked hardware interfaces.

skills.name: Build a hardware-in-the-loop test rig
skills.description: Build a rig where host scripts drive a real joint controller, inject sensor signals, bus faults and supply dips, and check responses and recovery automatically.

skills.name: Coordinate startup across many joint controllers
skills.description: Discover all joint controllers, check firmware versions and calibration, and bring them to enabled state together with clear failure reporting.

skills.name: Scope of human-robot interaction
skills.description: Explain what human-robot interaction studies, why social robots differ from industrial ones, and which factors (usefulness, ease, social fit) drive whether people accept a robot.

skills.name: Users' mental models of robots
skills.description: Explain how people form mental models of what a robot perceives, knows and can do, and predict misunderstandings when the robot's behavior contradicts those models.

skills.name: Anthropomorphism and social attribution
skills.description: Describe how humanlike form, voice and motion lead people to attribute intentions, emotions and agency to a robot, and when this helps or misleads interaction.

skills.name: Uncanny valley effect
skills.description: Explain the uncanny valley hypothesis, the evidence for and against it, and how mismatched realism between face, motion and voice produces discomfort.

skills.name: Stylized versus realistic humanoid design
skills.description: Choose a stylized or realistic appearance for a humanoid head and body, justifying the choice by cost, uncanny risk, expressiveness and the robot's intended role.

skills.name: Matching appearance to capability
skills.description: Identify the expectation gap created when a robot looks or sounds more capable than it is, and adjust form, voice and wording to keep expectations accurate.

skills.name: Trust and trust calibration
skills.description: Distinguish overtrust, undertrust and calibrated trust, list the robot behaviors and failures that shift trust, and propose measures that keep user trust matched to reliability.

skills.name: Design an HRI user study
skills.description: Design a within- or between-subjects study with a hypothesis, conditions, counterbalancing, sample size reasoning and informed-consent procedure for testing a robot behavior.

skills.name: Wizard-of-Oz prototyping
skills.description: Run a Wizard-of-Oz session where a hidden operator drives robot speech or motion, so interaction designs can be tested before autonomy exists, and disclose it appropriately.

skills.name: Score the Godspeed questionnaire
skills.description: Administer the Godspeed series (anthropomorphism, animacy, likeability, intelligence, safety), compute subscale scores and internal consistency, and compare conditions.

skills.name: Code observed interactions from video
skills.description: Build a coding scheme for observed interaction events, annotate recorded sessions with two raters, and compute inter-rater agreement such as Cohen's kappa.

skills.name: A/B test an interaction behavior
skills.description: Run an A/B comparison of two robot behaviors on a logged outcome such as task success or engagement time, and test whether the difference is statistically meaningful.

skills.name: Legible and predictable robot motion
skills.description: Distinguish predictable motion from legible motion, and shape arm and base trajectories so observers can infer the robot's goal early, trading efficiency against readability.

skills.name: Animation principles for robots
skills.description: Explain the classic animation principles (timing, anticipation, slow-in and slow-out, follow-through, arcs, exaggeration) and how each applies to a physical robot with joint limits.

skills.name: Easing curves and slow-in/slow-out
skills.description: Implement ease-in, ease-out and minimum-jerk easing functions for a joint move, and compare their velocity and acceleration profiles against a linear interpolation.

skills.name: Timing and speed to convey intent
skills.description: Choose motion speed, pauses and hold times so a gesture reads as calm, urgent, hesitant or confident, and verify the intended impression with observers.

skills.name: Anticipation before robot actions
skills.description: Add a short preparatory motion or gaze shift before a main action so observers can foresee what the robot will do, without violating workspace or safety limits.

skills.name: Follow-through and secondary motion
skills.description: Add follow-through, overlapping action and subtle secondary or idle motion (settling, breathing sway) so a robot appears alive without distracting jitter.

skills.name: Keyframe a robot joint animation
skills.description: Define keyframes for several joints, interpolate between them with easing, and play the result back as a time-stamped joint trajectory on a simulated robot.

skills.name: Author robot animations in a 3D tool
skills.description: Rig a robot model from its URDF in a 3D animation tool such as Blender, keyframe a gesture, and export it as joint trajectories the robot can play.

skills.name: Check animations against joint limits
skills.description: Check an authored animation for position, velocity, acceleration and torque limit violations, then retime or rescale it so the physical robot can execute it safely.

skills.name: Blend animations with live control
skills.description: Crossfade between animation clips and layer additive gestures over live control targets such as look-at or base motion, avoiding discontinuities at transitions.

skills.name: Functions of gaze in interaction
skills.description: Explain how gaze signals attention, regulates turn-taking, expresses intimacy through mutual gaze, and uses aversion while thinking, with typical durations from human studies.

skills.name: Compute head pan and tilt to look at a point
skills.description: Transform a 3D target point into the head frame and compute pan and tilt angles, respecting neck joint limits, so the robot's face points at the target.

skills.name: Eye-head coordination
skills.description: Coordinate fast eye movements with slower head turns so gaze lands quickly on a target and the head follows, keeping eyes centered and motion natural.

skills.name: Gaze and head-turn behavior
skills.description: Implement a gaze controller that tracks the person being addressed, holds mutual gaze, averts appropriately, and shifts attention with head motion timed to look intentional.

skills.name: Orient toward the active speaker
skills.description: Fuse sound direction from a microphone array with tracked faces to decide who is speaking and turn the head toward them, with hysteresis to avoid flicking.

skills.name: Joint attention and gaze following
skills.description: Follow a person's gaze or pointing to the object they mean, look at it to confirm shared reference, and look back to the person to check understanding.

skills.name: Types of nonverbal gestures
skills.description: Classify gestures as deictic, iconic, metaphoric, beat or emblem, and describe what each contributes to spoken communication and how culture changes emblem meanings.

skills.name: Generate a deictic pointing gesture
skills.description: Compute an arm pose that points a finger or hand at a target object or location, coordinated with gaze, and check that observers identify the intended target.

skills.name: Build a parameterized gesture library
skills.description: Author a set of reusable gestures (wave, bow, shrug, open palm, nod) with parameters for amplitude, speed and handedness that can be triggered by name.

skills.name: Synchronize beat gestures with speech
skills.description: Use word or phoneme timings from text-to-speech to place gesture strokes on stressed syllables, compensating for actuator latency so motion lands on time.

skills.name: Plan co-speech behavior with markup
skills.description: Annotate generated utterances with behavior tags for gestures, gaze shifts and expressions, and schedule them against speech timing using a behavior markup scheme.

skills.name: Facial action units and basic expressions
skills.description: Describe expressions in terms of facial action units for brows, lids and mouth, and identify which few features carry most of the emotional signal for a simplified robot face.

skills.name: Design and render an animated screen face
skills.description: Design a stylized screen face with parameterized eyes, brows and mouth, and render it at a steady frame rate with smooth eased transitions between poses.

skills.name: Drive LED eyes
skills.description: Build LED-matrix or addressable-LED eyes and drive them from a microcontroller with brightness, color and shape patterns for blinking, looking and simple emotions.

skills.name: Build an animatronic eye mechanism
skills.description: Design and assemble a servo-driven eye mechanism with pan, tilt and eyelids, choosing linkages and servos for range, speed and quiet operation.

skills.name: Blink, eyelid and brow behavior
skills.description: Generate natural blink timing from a random-interval model, link blinks to gaze shifts, and use lid and brow positions to express attention, surprise and concern.

skills.name: Mouth sync with visemes
skills.description: Map phonemes to visemes and drive mouth shapes from text-to-speech timing or audio amplitude, keeping lip motion aligned with speech audio within perceptual tolerance.

skills.name: Emotion models for robot expression
skills.description: Compare categorical emotion sets with dimensional models such as valence-arousal and pleasure-arousal-dominance, and choose one suited to driving robot expression.

skills.name: Implement an affect state with decay
skills.description: Implement an internal affect state that events push in valence-arousal space and that decays exponentially toward a neutral baseline, with bounded and testable outputs.

skills.name: Expressive face display
skills.description: Integrate affect-driven expressions, blinks, gaze and lip sync into one face controller that blends layers cleanly and stays readable during speech and motion.

skills.name: Write a robot character bible
skills.description: Write a character specification for the robot covering role, traits, values, speech style, humor limits and taboo topics, consistent with its capabilities and appearance.

skills.name: Select and tune a robot voice
skills.description: Select a text-to-speech voice and tune rate, pitch and prosody so the voice fits the character, stays intelligible in noise, and matches the robot's apparent size and age.

skills.name: Voice and personality design
skills.description: Implement the robot's persona as a language-model system prompt, voice settings and expression defaults, and verify replies stay in character across typical requests.

skills.name: Test consistent character across modalities
skills.description: Build a test set of prompts and situations, and check that words, voice, face and gesture express the same persona and emotion without contradiction over long sessions.

skills.name: Proxemic zones and personal space
skills.description: Describe intimate, personal, social and public distance zones, how culture, age and context shift them, and why a robot should treat them as soft constraints.

skills.name: Approach direction and speed
skills.description: Choose an approach path that keeps the robot visible, arrives from a front-oblique angle, and slows smoothly when entering a person's social zone.

skills.name: Robot height, posture and perceived dominance
skills.description: Explain how robot height and posture affect perceived dominance and comfort, and adjust torso height or lean to meet seated people and children at eye level.

skills.name: Proxemics and approach behavior
skills.description: Compute a goal pose near a tracked person from their position and facing, at a chosen social distance and angle, and drive the base there with proxemic speed limits.

skills.name: Social costmap layer around people
skills.description: Add a costmap layer that places asymmetric Gaussian costs around tracked people, larger in front than behind, so the planner keeps socially comfortable clearance.

skills.name: Navigate socially among people
skills.description: Navigate through spaces with moving people by passing on the expected side, yielding at doorways, not cutting through conversing groups, and signaling intent early.

skills.name: F-formations and joining groups
skills.description: Detect conversational group formations from people's positions and orientations, and choose where to stand to join or address a group without breaking its shared space.

skills.name: Detect user engagement
skills.description: Estimate whether a person intends to interact from distance, approach trajectory, face orientation and dwell time, and output a calibrated engagement score.

skills.name: Initiate interaction with a greeting
skills.description: Trigger a greeting when engagement is likely, using gaze, a gesture and a short utterance at the right distance, and back off gracefully if the person is not interested.

skills.name: End interactions gracefully
skills.description: Recognize pre-closing cues and disengagement, summarize or confirm outcomes, offer a farewell, and release attention without abruptly turning away.

skills.name: Multimodal turn-taking cues
skills.description: Signal holding or yielding the floor with gaze, pauses, prosody and gesture, and mask processing delays with brief thinking cues so users know when to speak.

skills.name: Backchannel while listening
skills.description: Produce nods and short vocalizations at pauses while the user speaks, timed from voice activity and prosody, so the user feels heard without being interrupted.

skills.name: Handle user interruptions
skills.description: Detect when a user speaks over the robot, stop or pause speech and gesture within a short latency, and resume or replan the reply appropriately.

skills.name: Multi-party conversation and addressee selection
skills.description: Track several participants, decide who is addressing the robot and whom to address, and distribute gaze and turns fairly in a group conversation.

skills.name: Politeness strategies for robots
skills.description: Apply politeness theory to phrase robot requests, refusals and corrections with suitable directness, hedging and deference for the relationship and situation.

skills.name: Greetings and gestures across cultures
skills.description: Describe greeting customs (bow, wave, handshake, verbal forms) and gesture meanings across major cultures, and choose robot greetings that avoid offense or unwanted touch.

skills.name: Formal address, titles and honorifics
skills.description: Address people with correct titles, honorifics and name order across languages, ask for preferred names, and switch formality appropriately as a relationship develops.

skills.name: Perform introductions between people
skills.description: Introduce people to each other following protocol on order, names, titles and context, and introduce the robot itself with an honest statement of its role.

skills.name: Implement configurable etiquette profiles
skills.description: Encode cultural and situational etiquette rules (greeting form, address, distance, formality) as configurable profiles that the dialogue and behavior layers consult.

skills.name: Signal robot state with light and sound
skills.description: Design consistent light, sound and on-screen cues for states such as idle, listening, thinking, moving and fault, so users can read the robot's state at a glance.

skills.name: Types of interaction failure
skills.description: Classify interaction breakdowns such as misrecognition, misunderstanding, unmet expectation and task failure, and identify the cues that reveal each during a conversation.

skills.name: Ask for clarification and confirm
skills.description: Choose between acting, implicit confirmation, explicit confirmation and clarification questions based on recognition confidence and the cost of a wrong action.

skills.name: Apology and trust repair after errors
skills.description: Choose apology, explanation and corrective-action strategies after a robot mistake, and evaluate how each affects user trust and willingness to continue.

skills.name: Announce and explain robot intentions
skills.description: Generate short spoken announcements of what the robot is about to do and why, timed before motion, using the planned action from the tool-calling layer.

skills.name: Communicate capability limits and uncertainty
skills.description: Tell users clearly what the robot cannot do or is unsure about, offer alternatives, and avoid overstating competence in ways that would miscalibrate trust.

skills.name: Accessible interaction design principles
skills.description: Apply inclusive design for hearing, vision, motor and cognitive differences, providing redundant output channels and alternative inputs such as touch or buttons.

skills.name: Live captions and visual speech feedback
skills.description: Display live captions of what the robot says and what it heard, so users can verify recognition and follow speech in noisy places or with hearing loss.

skills.name: Plain language and adjustable speech
skills.description: Rewrite robot utterances in plain language, short sentences and concrete words, and let users slow speech, repeat or simplify replies on request.

skills.name: Mobility-aware interaction
skills.description: Adapt approach, height, reach and handover positions for wheelchair users and people with limited mobility, keeping interaction points within comfortable reach.

skills.name: Hardware camera and microphone indicators
skills.description: Wire camera and microphone status lights so they are driven by sensor power and cannot be disabled in software, and add physical mute switches or shutters.

skills.name: Interaction data handling and minimization
skills.description: Decide what audio, video, transcripts and face data to keep, process on-device where possible, set retention limits, and document who can access stored data.

skills.name: Obtain consent in conversation
skills.description: Ask for, record and honor consent for recording, face enrollment or remembering personal details within a dialogue, including easy withdrawal and deletion.

skills.name: Interaction considerations for children
skills.description: Adapt robot speech, height, pacing and content for children, and apply safeguards against deception, over-attachment, data collection and unsupervised physical contact.

skills.name: Interaction considerations for older adults
skills.description: Adapt for hearing and vision changes, slower pacing, mobility aids and possible cognitive decline, while respecting dignity and avoiding patronizing or deceptive behavior.

skills.name: Warning signals before motion
skills.description: Precede potentially hazardous motion with audible and visual warnings and verbal notice, timed and scaled to the hazard identified in the risk assessment.

skills.name: Speed and separation near people
skills.description: Compute speed limits from separation distance and allowable contact energy, using power-and-force-limiting concepts, and slow or stop the robot as a person approaches.

skills.name: Stop or comply when touched
skills.description: Detect unexpected contact from torque residuals or touch sensors and respond within a bounded time by stopping or becoming compliant, then explain what happened.

skills.name: Social cues for object handover
skills.description: Use reach posture, gaze to the hand and object, and timed release so a person knows when and where to take an object handed over by the robot.

skills.name: Politely refuse unsafe requests
skills.description: Decline commands blocked by safety or policy guardrails with a polite explanation and a safe alternative, without arguing, lecturing or revealing exploitable details.

skills.name: Arbitrate behaviors across modalities
skills.description: Arbitrate competing requests for head, arms, face and voice by priority and resource locking, so safety, conversation and idle behaviors never fight over the same joints.

skills.name: Full spoken interaction loop with gesture and gaze
skills.description: Integrate listening, dialogue, speech, gaze, face and co-speech gesture into one real-time loop with turn-taking, repair and latency budgets measured end to end.

skills.name: Evaluate a deployed protocol droid
skills.description: Run an in-the-wild evaluation of the integrated robot with logged interactions, observation coding and questionnaires, and turn findings into prioritized design changes.

skills.name: Mobile base drive types compared
skills.description: Compare differential, skid-steer, mecanum, omni and swerve drives on maneuverability, holonomy, traction, floor sensitivity, cost and odometry quality to choose a base for an indoor humanoid.

skills.name: Differential-drive kinematics and wheel odometry
skills.description: Implement forward and inverse differential-drive kinematics in code and integrate encoder ticks into a timestamped pose and twist estimate published for the rest of the robot.

skills.name: Convert body twist commands to wheel speeds
skills.description: Accept a linear and angular body velocity command and convert it into left and right wheel angular velocities with correct units, signs and frame conventions.

skills.name: Skid-steer kinematics and effective track width
skills.description: Model a four-wheel skid-steer base as a differential drive with an empirically identified effective track width and explain the turning scrub it causes.

skills.name: Mecanum wheel kinematics
skills.description: Derive the four-wheel mecanum kinematic matrix mapping body twist to wheel speeds and its pseudoinverse for odometry, including roller angle and sign conventions.

skills.name: Select drive wheels and casters
skills.description: Choose wheel diameter, tread material, durometer and load rating plus caster size and swivel offset for a given floor type, payload and obstacle height.

skills.name: Traction-limited base acceleration
skills.description: Calculate the maximum acceleration and braking a wheeled base can achieve before drive wheels slip, using normal load on driven wheels and the friction coefficient.

skills.name: Size base drive motors
skills.description: Size drive motor torque, speed and gear ratio from robot mass, target speed, acceleration, ramp grade and rolling resistance coefficient, with a stated margin and duty cycle.

skills.name: Drive a base with BLDC hub motors
skills.description: Select brushless hub motors and matching field-oriented controllers for a mobile base and command them in velocity mode with correct direction, limits and encoder feedback.

skills.name: Wheel suspension to keep traction
skills.description: Explain why a rigid base with four or more wheels can lift a drive wheel on uneven floors and design a rocker or sprung suspension that keeps drive wheels loaded.

skills.name: Lay out a wheeled base chassis
skills.description: Lay out a mobile base chassis in CAD placing motors, wheels, battery, electronics and the upper-body mount to keep the center of mass low and service access clear.

skills.name: Closed-loop wheel velocity control
skills.description: Implement and tune a per-wheel velocity PI loop using encoder speed estimates, feedforward from the motor model and output saturation handling.

skills.name: Base velocity, acceleration and jerk limits
skills.description: Apply velocity, acceleration and jerk limits with a velocity smoother, scaling saturated wheel commands so path curvature is preserved and motion stays within traction bounds.

skills.name: Stop on stale velocity commands
skills.description: Implement a command timeout that ramps the base to zero velocity when no fresh command arrives within a set interval and logs the event.

skills.name: Configure ros2_control for a mobile base
skills.description: Write a ros2_control hardware interface for the base motors and configure the diff-drive controller with wheel geometry, limits and odometry publishing.

skills.name: Bring up a mobile base on blocks
skills.description: Commission a new base with wheels off the ground, verifying motor direction, encoder sign, odometry scale, command timeout and e-stop before driving on the floor.

skills.name: Teleoperate a base with a deadman switch
skills.description: Drive the base from a gamepad through a teleop node that requires a held deadman button, applies speed limits and stops when the controller disconnects.

skills.name: Odometry error growth and its sources
skills.description: Separate systematic odometry errors such as wheel diameter mismatch from random errors such as wheel slip, and show how small heading errors make position error grow with distance.

skills.name: Calibrate odometry with a square-path test
skills.description: Run clockwise and counterclockwise square-path trials, measure end-point errors and correct wheel diameter ratio and effective track width to reduce systematic drift.

skills.name: Fuse wheel odometry with an IMU
skills.description: Configure an extended Kalman filter node to fuse wheel odometry velocities with IMU yaw rate, setting covariances so heading drift is reduced without double counting.

skills.name: Base stopping distance
skills.description: Calculate stopping distance from speed, detection and actuation latency and achievable deceleration, and use it to set a safe maximum speed for a sensing range.

skills.name: Bumpers, cliff sensors and protective stop
skills.description: Fit contact bumpers and cliff sensors to a base and wire them into a protective stop that halts the drive independently of the navigation software.

skills.name: Static stability and the support polygon
skills.description: Construct the support polygon from ground contact points and judge static stability by whether the ground projection of the center of mass lies inside it, with a margin.

skills.name: Combined center of mass of a tall robot
skills.description: Compute the three-dimensional center of mass of a base carrying a torso, arms, head and battery from component masses and positions, and report its height.

skills.name: Static tip-over angle
skills.description: Calculate the tilt angle at which a wheeled robot tips about each support polygon edge from center of mass height and horizontal distance to that edge.

skills.name: Tip-over limit under acceleration
skills.description: Calculate the largest braking, acceleration or turning lateral acceleration before a tall robot tips, using the ratio of edge distance to center of mass height.

skills.name: Center of mass shift with arms and payload
skills.description: Compute how center of mass and stability margin change as arms extend or lift a payload, using forward kinematics over sampled arm configurations.

skills.name: Stability-aware base acceleration limits
skills.description: Scale base speed and acceleration limits online from the current arm pose and payload so the predicted tip-over margin never drops below a set threshold.

skills.name: Stability on ramps
skills.description: Combine ramp grade with braking and turning acceleration to find the worst-case stability margin of a tall wheeled robot on a ramp, uphill, downhill and across.

skills.name: Verify tip-over margin physically
skills.description: Measure a real robot's tip-over margin with a tilt platform or calibrated pull test in its worst configuration, using tethers, and compare with the predicted value.

skills.name: Speed and separation limits near people
skills.description: Define speed zones and protective fields so the base slows near people and stops before contact, from stopping distance, sensing range and approach behavior.

skills.name: Apply mobile robot safety standards
skills.description: Extract applicable requirements from mobile robot safety standards such as ISO 3691-4 and ANSI/RIA R15.08 and map them to measurable requirements for the base.

skills.name: Build a 2D map of a building
skills.description: Drive the base through a building while running a 2D lidar SLAM package, then save, inspect and clean the resulting occupancy grid for navigation use.

skills.name: Map, odom and base frame conventions
skills.description: Explain the map to odom to base_link frame chain, which node publishes each transform, and why odometry is continuous while map corrections may jump.

skills.name: Particle filter localization
skills.description: Implement Monte Carlo localization by sampling particles from a noisy odometry motion model, weighting them with a likelihood-field lidar model and applying low-variance resampling.

skills.name: Tune AMCL localization
skills.description: Configure AMCL with initial pose, particle limits, motion noise and laser model parameters, judge quality from particle spread and scan alignment, and recover when localization is lost.

skills.name: Layered costmaps
skills.description: Configure static, obstacle, voxel and inflation layers in global and local costmaps and explain how sensor marking and clearing produce the final cost grid.

skills.name: Tune footprint and inflation
skills.description: Set the robot footprint polygon, inflation radius and cost scaling so paths keep a sensible clearance without blocking doorways the robot can physically fit through.

skills.name: Mark 3D obstacles for a tall robot
skills.description: Project depth camera or 3D lidar points into a voxel costmap so table tops, shelves and overhangs at torso and head height block the tall robot's path.

skills.name: Update footprint when arms extend
skills.description: Recompute and publish the navigation footprint when arms reach out or a payload is carried so planners and collision checks use the true occupied area.

skills.name: Global path planners on costmaps
skills.description: Run and compare Dijkstra, A-star and Theta-star planners on a costmap, explaining path cost, heuristics, smoothing and why planned paths hug or avoid walls.

skills.name: Regulated pure pursuit path following
skills.description: Implement pure pursuit by steering toward a lookahead point, then regulate speed near curves and obstacles and tune lookahead distance for stability.

skills.name: Dynamic window local planning
skills.description: Sample velocity commands inside the dynamic window set by acceleration limits, forward-simulate trajectories and score them for obstacle cost, path alignment and progress.

skills.name: Independent collision monitor
skills.description: Add a collision monitor between planner and base that slows or stops on raw sensor points inside configured zones, independent of costmap correctness.

skills.name: Navigate among moving people
skills.description: Feed tracked people with predicted motion into planning so the base yields, waits or passes with clearance instead of treating people as static obstacles.

skills.name: Socially aware navigation
skills.description: Apply passing-side conventions, corridor yielding, approach angles and speed reduction so a humanoid base moves legibly and politely around people.

skills.name: Bring up Nav2 in simulation
skills.description: Launch Nav2 with a parameter file, map and lifecycle-managed nodes on a simulated base, send a goal and diagnose missing transforms or inactive nodes.

skills.name: Behavior tree fundamentals
skills.description: Read and write behavior trees using sequence, fallback, decorator and action nodes, and explain tick semantics and running states compared with state machines.

skills.name: Customize Nav2 behavior trees
skills.description: Modify the Nav2 navigate-to-pose behavior tree to change replanning rate, order recovery behaviors such as spin, back-up and costmap clearing, and add custom action nodes.

skills.name: Autonomous navigation with Nav2
skills.description: Run Nav2 on the physical base so it localizes on a saved map, plans and follows paths to goals, avoids new obstacles and recovers when blocked.

skills.name: Measure navigation performance
skills.description: Run repeated navigation trials and report success rate, goal position and heading error, time to goal, interventions and near misses with logged data.

skills.name: Autonomous docking to a charger
skills.description: Approach a charging dock with navigation, switch to fiducial-guided final alignment and verify charging current, retrying when contact is not confirmed.

skills.name: Keepout and speed-limit zones
skills.description: Draw keepout and speed-limit masks over the map and apply them with costmap filters so the robot avoids stairs and slows in busy areas.

skills.name: Pass through doorways and narrow gaps
skills.description: Plan and execute passage through doorways and narrow gaps by aligning before entry, reducing speed and checking footprint clearance including extended arms.

skills.name: Cross thresholds and ramps
skills.description: Determine from wheel diameter, ground clearance and approach angle which thresholds and ramps a base can cross, then cross them at controlled speed with stability checks.

skills.name: Legged robot anatomy and degrees of freedom
skills.description: Identify the hip, knee and ankle joints of a humanoid leg, explain why six degrees of freedom per leg is typical and compare leg layouts.

skills.name: Leg forward and inverse kinematics
skills.description: Compute foot pose from leg joint angles and solve inverse kinematics analytically for a six-joint leg with intersecting hip axes, checking joint limits.

skills.name: Static versus dynamic stability
skills.description: Distinguish statically stable gaits, which keep the center of mass over the support polygon, from dynamic gaits that rely on motion and momentum to stay upright.

skills.name: Center of pressure
skills.description: Calculate the center of pressure from distributed vertical contact forces under one or two feet and relate it to the net ground reaction moment.

skills.name: Measure foot ground reaction forces
skills.description: Instrument a foot with force-sensitive resistors or load cells, calibrate them and compute total normal force and center of pressure in real time.

skills.name: Contact forces and friction cones
skills.description: Check whether a contact force lies inside its friction cone, linearize the cone as a pyramid and extend the idea to the contact wrench of a flat foot.

skills.name: Centroidal dynamics
skills.description: Relate contact forces to the rate of change of linear and angular momentum about the center of mass and compute centroidal momentum from joint velocities.

skills.name: Zero moment point balance criterion
skills.description: Compute the zero moment point from center of mass motion and judge whether a motion is dynamically feasible by whether the ZMP stays inside the support polygon.

skills.name: Linear inverted pendulum model
skills.description: Derive the linear inverted pendulum equations under constant center of mass height, solve them in closed form and simulate center of mass motion for a given ZMP.

skills.name: Capture point
skills.description: Compute the instantaneous capture point from center of mass position and velocity and decide whether the robot can stop by stepping or must take more steps.

skills.name: Divergent component of motion
skills.description: Split linear inverted pendulum dynamics into stable and divergent parts and plan DCM trajectories backward from final footsteps to drive walking.

skills.name: Ankle and hip balance strategies
skills.description: Implement ankle and hip strategies that shift the center of pressure or swing the upper body to keep a standing robot balanced after small pushes.

skills.name: Gait phases and timing
skills.description: Describe single support, double support, swing and stance phases, and set step period, duty factor and double-support ratio for a walking pattern.

skills.name: Footstep planning
skills.description: Generate a footstep sequence to a goal respecting step length, width, rotation and collision constraints, alternating feet and handling turning in place.

skills.name: Swing foot trajectories
skills.description: Generate smooth swing foot trajectories with polynomial or spline segments that meet clearance height and land with near-zero velocity at the planned footstep.

skills.name: Center of mass trajectory from footsteps
skills.description: Produce a center of mass trajectory from a footstep plan using ZMP or DCM references and convert it with swing trajectories into joint commands via leg IK.

skills.name: Push recovery by stepping
skills.description: Adjust the next footstep location and timing from the capture point so the robot recovers from pushes too large for ankle or hip strategies.

skills.name: Make a simulated biped walk
skills.description: Make a simulated biped stand, walk forward, turn and stop on flat ground using a model-based gait or a learned policy, with logged ZMP or stability margins.

skills.name: Foot contact detection
skills.description: Decide foot contact state from force sensors, estimated joint torques and gait phase, with hysteresis so early or late touchdown is handled cleanly.

skills.name: Legged state estimation
skills.description: Fuse IMU data with leg kinematics of feet in stance in a Kalman filter to estimate base velocity, orientation and position for walking control.

skills.name: Contact force distribution by optimization
skills.description: Formulate a quadratic program that distributes desired centroidal wrench across feet in contact while respecting friction cones and torque limits.

skills.name: Whole-body walking controller
skills.description: Combine center of mass or DCM tracking, swing foot tracking, torso posture and contact constraints in a prioritized whole-body controller that outputs joint torques.

skills.name: Model predictive control for walking
skills.description: Formulate a receding-horizon controller on a ZMP or centroidal model that replans center of mass motion and footstep positions every cycle under constraints.

skills.name: Locomotion reinforcement learning environment
skills.description: Set up a parallel simulated locomotion environment with observations, joint-target actions under PD control, command sampling, termination and reset conditions.

skills.name: Reward design for locomotion
skills.description: Design reward terms for velocity tracking, orientation, energy, joint limits, foot clearance and gait regularity, and diagnose reward hacking from rollouts.

skills.name: Train a locomotion policy with PPO
skills.description: Train a walking policy with PPO and a terrain or command curriculum, tracking returns, episode length and gait quality to decide when training has converged.

skills.name: Domain randomization for locomotion
skills.description: Randomize mass, friction, motor strength, latency, sensor noise and external pushes during training so a policy tolerates mismatch between simulation and hardware.

skills.name: Model actuator dynamics for sim-to-real
skills.description: Identify actuator bandwidth, torque limits, friction and latency from hardware logs and add them to simulation, or train an actuator network, to narrow the reality gap.

skills.name: Transfer a locomotion policy to hardware
skills.description: Deploy a trained locomotion policy on hardware at a fixed control rate, match observations and action scaling to simulation and gate it with torque and attitude limits.

skills.name: Detect an imminent fall
skills.description: Detect an unrecoverable fall early from capture point outside reachable footholds, trunk tilt and angular rate thresholds, and trigger a fall response.

skills.name: Safe falling
skills.description: Execute a fall response that crouches, turns toward padded surfaces, protects the head and joints with compliant control and manages motor power at impact.

skills.name: Get up after a fall
skills.description: Design and verify get-up motions from face-down and face-up positions, keeping joint torques within limits and the center of mass over changing support.

skills.name: Elevation mapping for footholds
skills.description: Build a local elevation map from depth data and score candidate footholds by flatness, slope and edge distance for the footstep planner.

skills.name: Walk on uneven ground
skills.description: Keep walking over small unexpected height changes using contact-timing adaptation, compliant ankles and posture correction rather than assuming flat ground.

skills.name: Walk on slopes and stairs
skills.description: Adapt foot orientation, swing clearance, step height and center of mass placement to walk up and down slopes and perceived stairs with friction margins.

skills.name: Leg actuator requirements from walking
skills.description: Extract peak and RMS joint torque, speed and power for each leg joint from simulated walking, stairs and falls to specify leg actuators.

skills.name: Design a humanoid leg
skills.description: Design a leg with proximal actuator placement, low distal mass, joint ranges for walking and getting up, and a foot sized for the support polygon needed.

skills.name: Safety harness and gantry testing
skills.description: Set up an overhead gantry or harness with fall-arrest slack, quick release and e-stop so legged experiments cannot damage the robot or people nearby.

skills.name: Biped hardware test progression
skills.description: Plan and run staged biped tests from suspended leg motions to supported standing, stepping in place, harnessed walking and finally free walking with exit criteria.

skills.name: Walk a physical biped
skills.description: Make a physical biped walk, turn and stop on flat floor for a set distance without the harness bearing load, logging falls, interventions and stability margins.

skills.name: Degrees of freedom needed for a manipulation task
skills.description: Explain why six independent joints are needed to place a tool at an arbitrary position and orientation, and what fewer or extra joints cost or buy for a given task.

skills.name: Common arm joint layouts
skills.description: Compare articulated, SCARA, Cartesian and cylindrical arm layouts by workspace shape, stiffness, singularities and suitability for desktop, industrial and humanoid use.

skills.name: Wrist types and wrist offsets
skills.description: Distinguish spherical, offset and roll-pitch-roll wrists, and explain how intersecting wrist axes simplify inverse kinematics while offset wrists trade that for packaging and range.

skills.name: Specify reach and workspace from the task envelope
skills.description: Derive required arm reach and workspace from table heights, shelf depths and torso position, and express them as measurable requirements a design can be checked against.

skills.name: Rated payload from joint torque limits
skills.description: Compute the payload an arm can hold at full extension from shoulder and elbow torque limits, link masses and a stated margin, identifying the limiting joint.

skills.name: Anthropomorphic 7-DOF arm layout
skills.description: Describe the shoulder-elbow-wrist layout of a human-like seven-joint arm, its elbow swivel angle, joint ranges and why it suits a humanoid working in human spaces.

skills.name: Choose a humanoid arm configuration under budgets
skills.description: Select joint count, wrist type, link lengths and actuator placement for a humanoid arm by trading reach, payload, mass, cost and inertia against written requirements.

skills.name: End-effector families and task fit
skills.description: Match parallel-jaw, adaptive, suction, magnetic and multi-finger end-effectors to object shape, material, surface and required precision, stating each family's main failure modes.

skills.name: Parallel-jaw gripper mechanisms
skills.description: Explain rack-and-pinion, lead-screw, parallelogram-linkage and cam mechanisms for parallel jaws, comparing stroke, force amplification, backdrivability and part count.

skills.name: Design finger pads and jaw geometry
skills.description: Choose fingertip shape, V-grooves and compliant elastomer pads to raise effective friction, center parts and tolerate pose error for a given object set.

skills.name: Adaptive underactuated grippers
skills.description: Explain how linkage or tendon fingers with fewer motors than joints wrap around irregular objects, and predict when they pinch instead of envelop.

skills.name: Size a vacuum suction gripper
skills.description: Calculate holding force from vacuum level and cup area, apply a safety factor for acceleration and peel loads, and choose cup material for porous or curved surfaces.

skills.name: Magnetic and electromagnetic grippers
skills.description: Explain holding force, air-gap sensitivity, residual magnetism and release behavior of permanent and electromagnetic grippers, and when ferrous-only handling is acceptable.

skills.name: Tool changers and end-effector interfaces
skills.description: Specify a standard tool flange, locking mechanism and power and signal pass-through so an arm can swap end-effectors repeatably and safely.

skills.name: Required grip force from friction
skills.description: Calculate the squeeze force a two-finger friction grasp needs to hold an object's weight, using the friction coefficient and number of contact surfaces.

skills.name: Grip margin under acceleration and tilt
skills.description: Extend grip-force calculations to include arm acceleration, tilted grasps and torque about the grasp axis from an off-center object, then apply a payload safety factor.

skills.name: Size a gripper actuator and transmission
skills.description: Work back from required jaw force through the gripper mechanism's mechanical advantage to motor torque, and decide whether the drive should self-lock on power loss.

skills.name: Position-controlled gripper opening and closing
skills.description: Calibrate jaw opening against motor position and command target widths with a servo or PID loop, handling the stall that occurs when jaws meet an object.

skills.name: Force-limited gripping through current limits
skills.description: Convert a desired jaw force into a motor current or torque limit and close the gripper under that limit so fragile objects are not crushed.

skills.name: Detect a successful grasp from width and current
skills.description: Classify a closing event as holding, missed or dropped from final jaw width, motor current and their change over time, and choose robust thresholds.

skills.name: Design and control a parallel-jaw gripper
skills.description: Design, print, assemble and wire a servo-driven parallel-jaw gripper, then command width and force and report grasp status to the arm controller.

skills.name: Contact models for grasping
skills.description: Distinguish frictionless point, point-with-friction and soft-finger contact models by the forces and torques each can transmit to a grasped object.

skills.name: Friction cones and their linear approximation
skills.description: Represent the set of allowable contact forces as a friction cone and approximate it with a polyhedral pyramid of edge vectors for computation.

skills.name: Antipodal grasps for two-finger grippers
skills.description: Test whether two contact points form an antipodal grasp by checking that the line between them lies inside both friction cones.

skills.name: Grasp matrix and contact wrenches
skills.description: Build the grasp matrix that maps contact forces to the net wrench on an object, using contact positions, normals and the chosen contact model.

skills.name: Form closure
skills.description: Determine whether a set of frictionless contacts geometrically immobilizes an object, and count the minimum contacts needed in the plane and in space.

skills.name: Force closure
skills.description: Test whether frictional contacts can resist any external wrench by checking that contact wrench cones positively span wrench space.

skills.name: Grasp quality metrics
skills.description: Compute and compare grasp quality measures such as the largest-minimum-resisted-wrench epsilon metric, wrench-space volume and grasp-matrix singular values.

skills.name: Represent a grasp as gripper pose and width
skills.description: Encode a candidate grasp as a six-DOF gripper frame plus opening width and approach axis, and transform it between camera, object and robot base frames.

skills.name: Top-down grasps from 2D detections and depth
skills.description: Turn a detected object's mask and depth into a top-down grasp by finding its center, principal axis yaw, height and required jaw width.

skills.name: Sample antipodal grasps from a point cloud
skills.description: Estimate surface normals in a segmented point cloud, sample point pairs that satisfy antipodal conditions, and convert them into six-DOF grasp candidates.

skills.name: Filter and rank grasp candidates
skills.description: Reject grasps whose gripper collides with the scene or has no inverse-kinematics solution, then rank survivors by quality, approach direction and joint-limit margin.

skills.name: Task-oriented grasp selection
skills.description: Choose where to grasp an object based on what happens next, such as holding a mug by the body to pour or by the handle to hand it over.

skills.name: Approach, pre-grasp and retreat poses
skills.description: Compute pre-grasp, grasp and retreat poses by offsetting the grasp frame along its approach axis and lifting clear of the support surface.

skills.name: Straight-line Cartesian approach moves
skills.description: Interpolate gripper poses along a straight line, solve inverse kinematics at each step, and reject paths with joint jumps, limit violations or singularities.

skills.name: Sequence a pick as a state machine
skills.description: Implement pick as perceive, plan, approach, grasp, verify and lift states with explicit failure transitions and timeouts at every step.

skills.name: Compute a stable place pose
skills.description: Choose a place pose that puts the object upright on a support surface with its center of mass over the base, a small release height and a clear retreat path.

skills.name: Vision-guided pick-and-place
skills.description: Integrate detection, hand-eye transforms, grasp selection, motion and gripper control so a desktop arm picks named objects and places them at target locations.

skills.name: Place objects accurately with an error budget
skills.description: Budget placement error from calibration, perception, grasp offset and slip, then reduce it by re-measuring the object pose in the hand before placing.

skills.name: Eye-in-hand versus eye-to-hand cameras
skills.description: Compare wrist-mounted and fixed external cameras by field of view, occlusion, calibration chain and accuracy near the grasp, and choose one for a task.

skills.name: Hand-eye calibration as AX = XB
skills.description: Write the transform loop linking robot poses, camera observations of a target and the unknown camera mount, and show why several varied poses are needed.

skills.name: Hand-eye calibration
skills.description: Collect robot poses with fiducial observations, solve for the camera-to-gripper or camera-to-base transform, publish it as a static transform, and verify it with tool-tip touch-off tests.

skills.name: Position-based visual servoing
skills.description: Close a feedback loop that drives the gripper toward a target pose estimated by the camera each frame, correcting calibration and model errors.

skills.name: Six-axis wrist force-torque sensors
skills.description: Explain how strain-gauge bridges and a calibration matrix give six-axis force and torque, and read range, resolution, overload and noise specifications.

skills.name: Remove bias and tool gravity from force-torque data
skills.description: Identify tool mass, center of mass and sensor bias from several static orientations, subtract them, and transform the remaining contact wrench to the tool tip frame.

skills.name: Detect contact from force thresholds
skills.description: Detect the moment of contact from compensated force signals using filtered thresholds set from measured noise, balancing missed contacts against false alarms.

skills.name: Estimate external force from joint currents
skills.description: Estimate external joint torques from motor currents minus modeled gravity and friction, then map them to an end-effector force with the Jacobian transpose.

skills.name: Tactile sensor technologies
skills.description: Compare resistive, capacitive, magnetic and camera-based tactile sensors by spatial resolution, bandwidth, durability, wiring and what contact information each provides.

skills.name: Detect and react to slip
skills.description: Detect incipient slip from tangential-to-normal force ratio or vibration signals and respond by increasing grip force before the object moves.

skills.name: Guarded moves that stop on contact
skills.description: Move slowly toward an expected surface and stop or switch behavior when contact is detected, to locate tables, buttons and object tops reliably.

skills.name: Admittance control for a position-controlled arm
skills.description: Convert measured contact forces into small position or velocity offsets so a stiff, position-controlled arm behaves like a tunable spring and damper.

skills.name: Compliant peg-in-hole insertion
skills.description: Insert a peg into a close-fitting hole using chamfers, compliance and spiral search, and diagnose jamming and wedging from force readings.

skills.name: Open doors and drawers
skills.description: Model a door as a revolute and a drawer as a prismatic constraint, grasp the handle, and pull compliantly while estimating the hinge axis or slide direction online.

skills.name: Use a held tool
skills.description: Define a tool frame for a grasped tool, apply controlled contact forces at its tip, and perform tasks such as wiping, pressing or scooping.

skills.name: Collaborative robot safety modes
skills.description: Explain safety-rated monitored stop, hand guiding, speed and separation monitoring, and power and force limiting as defined for collaborative robots in ISO 10218 and ISO/TS 15066.

skills.name: Power and force limits for human contact
skills.description: Estimate an arm's effective moving mass and permissible speed so a possible contact with each body region stays within published force and pressure limits.

skills.name: Speed and separation monitoring
skills.description: Compute a protective separation distance from human and robot speeds, reaction and stopping times, and slow or stop the arm when a person comes closer.

skills.name: Detect collisions and react safely
skills.description: Detect unexpected arm contact from joint torque residuals and choose a safe reaction such as stopping, retracting or switching to compliant mode.

skills.name: Hand objects to and from a person
skills.description: Offer an object at a reachable, legible pose, release only when the person's pull is sensed, and receive objects by tracking the hand and confirming the grasp.

skills.name: Two-arm kinematics in a shared torso frame
skills.description: Model both arms in one robot description with a common torso frame, and compute the relative pose between the two hands.

skills.name: Closed-chain constraint of a shared object
skills.description: Derive the constraint that keeps both hands' relative pose fixed when they rigidly hold one object, and compute compatible joint velocities for both arms.

skills.name: Internal squeeze force in two-hand grasps
skills.description: Separate the wrench that moves a jointly held object from the internal squeeze force, and regulate squeeze with compliance so the object is neither dropped nor crushed.

skills.name: Plan dual-arm motion without self-collision
skills.description: Plan motions for both arms together so they avoid each other, the torso and the head while meeting timing for coordinated tasks.

skills.name: Bimanual coordination
skills.description: Classify two-handed tasks as independent, asymmetric or shared-object, and coordinate two arms on them, such as holding a jar while opening it or lifting a tray, with synchronized timing and force control.

skills.name: Carry an object with two hands
skills.description: Lift and carry a box or tray with both hands, checking combined payload, squeeze margin and level orientation while the torso or base moves.

skills.name: Human hand anatomy and grasp taxonomy
skills.description: Describe human finger and thumb joints and classify grasps into power, precision and intermediate types to set functional goals for a robot hand.

skills.name: Finger kinematics
skills.description: Compute fingertip position from MCP, PIP and DIP joint angles, including coupled distal joints, and map each finger's reachable workspace.

skills.name: Thumb opposition and placement
skills.description: Choose thumb base location and joint axes so the thumb tip can oppose each fingertip, and check opposition reach with a kinematic model.

skills.name: Tendon-driven finger design
skills.description: Design tendon routing, pulley radii and return springs or antagonist tendons, and compute joint torques from tendon tension and moment arms.

skills.name: Linkage-driven finger design
skills.description: Design a four-bar or multi-bar linkage that couples finger joints to one actuator, and check the resulting curl trajectory and fingertip force.

skills.name: Underactuated fingers and differentials
skills.description: Use springs and differential mechanisms so fewer actuators drive more joints, and predict how fingers adapt their shape to objects of different sizes.

skills.name: Sensing in a robot hand
skills.description: Select and integrate joint-angle, motor-current, tendon-tension and fingertip tactile sensing within the wiring and space limits of a compact hand.

skills.name: Dexterous multi-finger hand
skills.description: Design, build and control a multi-finger hand with an opposable thumb, then execute power, pinch and tripod grasps under force limits to meet grasp and payload goals.

skills.name: In-hand manipulation
skills.description: Reposition an object within the hand by finger gaiting, rolling and controlled sliding, keeping the grasp stable while contacts change.

skills.name: Teleoperation mappings
skills.description: Compare joint-space mapping from a matching leader arm with Cartesian mapping from a pose device, including frame alignment and workspace scaling.

skills.name: Build a leader-follower arm pair
skills.description: Assemble and calibrate a leader-follower arm pair such as LeRobot SO-101, aligning joint zeros and directions so the follower mirrors the leader.

skills.name: Teleoperate an arm to record demonstrations
skills.description: Teleoperate an arm through a task smoothly while synchronously recording camera images, joint states and commanded actions with consistent timestamps.

skills.name: Teleoperate with a VR headset and controllers
skills.description: Stream VR controller poses into the robot frame, map them to hand targets through inverse kinematics, and add deadman switches and workspace limits.

skills.name: Retarget human hand motion to a robot hand
skills.description: Map data-glove or camera hand-tracking joint angles to a robot hand with different proportions, preserving fingertip contact and pinch distances.

skills.name: Structure a demonstration episode
skills.description: Define an episode's observations, actions, timestamps, task label and success flag, and store it in a standard format such as a LeRobot dataset.

skills.name: Choose observation and action spaces
skills.description: Choose between absolute joint, delta joint and end-effector actions, select camera views and proprioception, and normalize them consistently for training.

skills.name: Write a demonstration collection protocol
skills.description: Plan how many episodes to record, how to vary object poses, lighting and distractors, and how operators keep a consistent strategy.

skills.name: Audit and clean a demonstration dataset
skills.description: Find dropped frames, timestamp drift, failed or inconsistent episodes and camera changes, then split train and validation by session to avoid leakage.

skills.name: Behavior cloning as supervised learning
skills.description: Train a policy that regresses demonstrated actions from observations, and explain why compounding error and covariate shift make low validation loss a weak predictor of task success.

skills.name: Multimodal action distributions
skills.description: Explain why averaging demonstrations that pass left or right of an obstacle produces a colliding action, and which policy classes model several modes.

skills.name: Action chunking with transformers
skills.description: Train an ACT policy that predicts chunks of future actions with a transformer and temporal ensembling, and tune chunk size and inputs.

skills.name: Diffusion policy for visuomotor control
skills.description: Train a policy that generates action sequences by iterative denoising conditioned on images, and trade denoising steps against control latency.

skills.name: Train an imitation-learning manipulation policy
skills.description: Collect, clean and train on demonstrations for a real manipulation task, then deploy the policy and iterate until it meets a stated success target.

skills.name: Run a learned policy on the robot safely
skills.description: Run policy inference at control rate on robot hardware with action clipping, workspace limits and a human stop, logging every rollout for review.

skills.name: Success rates with confidence intervals
skills.description: Estimate a task success rate from repeated trials with a binomial confidence interval, and decide how many trials are needed to compare two systems.

skills.name: Design a fair manipulation evaluation protocol
skills.description: Fix initial conditions, trial counts, success criteria and partial-credit rubrics so different policies or pipelines are compared on equal terms.

skills.name: Test generalization of manipulation policies
skills.description: Measure performance on unseen object instances, positions, lighting and backgrounds, separating in-distribution from out-of-distribution results.

skills.name: Tip-over check when reaching from a wheeled base
skills.description: Check that the combined center of mass of base, torso, arm and payload stays inside the support polygon with margin at full reach and during braking.

skills.name: Manipulate with the base stationary
skills.description: Navigate to a base pose, stop and hold position, re-perceive the target from the new viewpoint, then pick or place before moving again.

skills.name: Reach while the base is moving
skills.description: Coordinate base and arm motion so the hand tracks a target while the base moves, accounting for base odometry error and arm workspace limits.

skills.name: Sketch lines, arcs and circles on a plane
skills.description: Create a new part, choose a sketch plane and draw lines, arcs, circles and rectangles anchored to the origin in a parametric CAD tool.

skills.name: Constrain and fully define a sketch
skills.description: Apply geometric relations and driving dimensions until a sketch is fully defined, and diagnose under-defined or conflicting constraints without losing design intent.

skills.name: Sketch, constrain and extrude a part in parametric CAD
skills.description: Turn a fully constrained sketch into a solid using boss and cut extrudes with blind, through-all and up-to-face end conditions to model a simple bracket.

skills.name: Reference planes, axes and coordinate systems
skills.description: Create offset and angled reference planes, axes and part coordinate systems to place features and define the frame used later for kinematics.

skills.name: Revolve, sweep and loft features
skills.description: Model axisymmetric parts with revolves, path-following parts with sweeps, and transitional shapes with lofts, choosing the right feature for each geometry.

skills.name: Fillets, shells, patterns and mirrors
skills.description: Add fillets, chamfers, shells, drafts, patterns and mirrors in a robust order so bolt circles and ribs repeat from one editable source feature.

skills.name: Plan feature order and design intent
skills.description: Choose base features, references and feature order so that likely design changes propagate predictably instead of breaking downstream features.

skills.name: Variables, equations and design tables
skills.description: Drive dimensions from global variables and equations, then use configurations or a design table to generate a family of sized parts from one model.

skills.name: Mass properties from a CAD model
skills.description: Assign materials and densities, then read mass, centre of mass and inertia tensor about a chosen frame and check them against hand estimates.

skills.name: Constrain components with assembly mates
skills.description: Insert components and constrain them with coincident, concentric, distance and angle mates, then count the remaining degrees of freedom of each part.

skills.name: Build a CAD assembly with mates and motion
skills.description: Assemble a multi-part mechanism with fixed ground, subassemblies and limited angle mates so it moves only through its intended joint range.

skills.name: Interference checks and motion studies
skills.description: Drive assembly joints through their range in a motion study, detecting interference and minimum clearance at each pose before parts are made.

skills.name: Bill of materials, part numbers and revisions
skills.description: Generate a bill of materials from an assembly, apply a part numbering and revision scheme, and keep CAD files traceable to built hardware.

skills.name: Export STEP, STL and DXF correctly
skills.description: Export neutral STEP for exchange, STL or 3MF meshes at suitable resolution for printing, and DXF profiles at true scale for cutting services.

skills.name: Export a CAD assembly to a robot description
skills.description: Export link meshes, joint frames, masses and inertias from a CAD assembly into a URDF and check frames and inertias against the model.

skills.name: Surface modeling with curvature continuity
skills.description: Build freeform surfaces with boundary and loft surfaces, check G1 and G2 continuity with zebra analysis, and knit them into solids for shells.

skills.name: Orthographic, section and detail views
skills.description: Read and lay out third- and first-angle orthographic projections with section, detail and auxiliary views that fully describe a part's geometry.

skills.name: Dimensioning practice on drawings
skills.description: Dimension a part from functional features using baseline and ordinate schemes, avoid redundant dimensions, and note hole and thread callouts correctly.

skills.name: Create a drawing from a CAD model
skills.description: Generate a drawing sheet from a CAD part with title block, material, finish, general tolerances, notes and revision block ready to send to a shop.

skills.name: Tolerance notation and general tolerances
skills.description: Interpret limit, bilateral and unilateral tolerances and general tolerance tables such as ISO 2768, and compute the allowed size range of a feature.

skills.name: Select ISO limits and fits
skills.description: Choose hole-basis clearance, transition and interference fits such as H7/g6 or H7/p6 and compute the minimum and maximum clearance from tables.

skills.name: Datum reference frames and feature control frames
skills.description: Read a feature control frame, identify primary, secondary and tertiary datums, and explain how the part is constrained when measured.

skills.name: Form and orientation tolerances
skills.description: Apply and interpret flatness, straightness, perpendicularity and parallelism tolerances, and choose them for bearing seats and mounting faces.

skills.name: Position tolerance and bonus tolerance
skills.description: Calculate positional tolerance zones for bolt patterns, including material-condition modifiers and bonus tolerance, and check fastener fit using the floating-fastener formula.

skills.name: Worst-case and statistical tolerance stacks
skills.description: Compute a one-dimensional tolerance stack both worst-case and by root-sum-square, and decide which applies to a bearing preload or gear mesh gap.

skills.name: Thread standards and designations
skills.description: Read metric and Unified thread designations, pitch, thread class and length, and identify a screw with a thread gauge and calipers.

skills.name: Choose screw heads, nuts and washers
skills.description: Select socket head, button, flat and set screws, nuts, nylon-insert locknuts and washers by access, head height, clamping area and tool clearance.

skills.name: Thread engagement length and stripping
skills.description: Calculate the thread engagement needed so a bolt breaks before threads strip in steel, aluminum or plastic, and size tapped hole depth accordingly.

skills.name: Bolt preload from tightening torque
skills.description: Estimate bolt preload from tightening torque with the nut-factor relation, choose a target preload as a fraction of proof load, and set torque specifications.

skills.name: Size and design a bolted joint
skills.description: Size bolts for a robot bracket under shear and separating loads, using preload, joint stiffness, friction-grip capacity and a safety factor.

skills.name: Prevent fastener loosening under vibration
skills.description: Explain transverse-slip self-loosening and choose threadlocker grade, prevailing-torque nuts, wedge washers or safety wire for vibrating robot joints.

skills.name: Tap holes and install helical inserts
skills.description: Drill and tap threads in aluminum and plastic and install helical coil inserts where repeated assembly would wear soft threads.

skills.name: Design bosses for heat-set inserts in prints
skills.description: Size printed bosses and holes for brass heat-set inserts, install them square with a soldering tool, and test pull-out and torque-out strength.

skills.name: Locate parts with dowel pins
skills.description: Use a dowel pin in a round hole and a second pin in a slot to locate parts repeatably, choosing press and slip fits for each hole.

skills.name: Calculate interference press fits
skills.description: Compute contact pressure, holding torque and assembly force for a press fit from interference, part stiffness and friction, including printed and aluminum hubs.

skills.name: Size a shaft for combined loading and stiffness
skills.description: Combine bending and torsional stress with von Mises, then choose a shaft diameter meeting deflection limits and fatigue life at shoulders and keyways.

skills.name: Bearing types and their load directions
skills.description: Compare deep-groove, angular-contact, needle, tapered, thrust, crossed-roller and plain bearings by radial, axial and moment load capacity, size and stiffness.

skills.name: Fixed and floating bearing arrangements
skills.description: Arrange two bearings as fixed-floating or paired angular-contact in back-to-back or face-to-face layouts to carry moment loads without overconstraint.

skills.name: Bearing rating life calculation
skills.description: Compute equivalent dynamic load and L10 rating life from catalog ratings, and check static load capacity for shock and holding loads.

skills.name: Bearing seat fits and mounting practice
skills.description: Pick shaft and housing tolerances for rotating and stationary rings, design shoulder heights, and press bearings in without loading through the balls.

skills.name: Bearing preload methods
skills.description: Apply bearing preload with wave springs, shims or ground spacers, and explain the trade between joint stiffness, play and friction torque.

skills.name: Select and mount bearings for a rotating joint
