skills.description: Plot omnidirectional, cardioid and figure-eight polar patterns in polar coordinates and predict off-axis rejection of robot self-noise.

skills.name: Moving-coil loudspeaker principles
skills.description: Explain how voice-coil force on a cone radiates sound, why small drivers lose bass, and why front and rear waves cancel without a baffle.

skills.name: Loudspeaker sensitivity and required amplifier power
skills.description: Use speaker sensitivity in dB at 1 W and 1 m with distance loss to find the amplifier power needed for a target speech level at a listener.

skills.name: Loudspeaker enclosures and Helmholtz ports
skills.description: Explain sealed and ported speaker enclosures, compute a Helmholtz port resonance, and judge how a head shell affects voice quality and echo.

skills.name: Instantaneous field of view and object-space pixel size
skills.description: Compute the angle each pixel subtends from pixel pitch and focal length, and the millimeters per pixel at a working distance for manipulation tasks.

skills.name: f-number, aperture area and exposure stops
skills.description: Relate f-number to aperture diameter and light gathering, showing each full stop halves image-plane irradiance and scales with f-number squared.

skills.name: Depth of field and circle of confusion
skills.description: Compute near and far limits of acceptable focus and the hyperfocal distance from focal length, f-number and an allowable circle of confusion.

skills.name: Diffraction blur versus pixel size
skills.description: Compute the Airy disk diameter from wavelength and f-number, compare it with pixel pitch, and find the aperture beyond which diffraction limits sharpness.

skills.name: Chromatic and spherical aberrations
skills.description: Explain physically how dispersion and spherical surfaces blur images, and why stopping down, achromatic doublets and aspheric elements reduce these errors.

skills.name: Physical origin of barrel and pincushion distortion
skills.description: Explain how aperture stop position and wide-angle projection bend straight lines into barrel or pincushion shapes, and contrast rectilinear and fisheye mappings.

skills.name: Photon shot noise and signal-to-noise ratio
skills.description: Estimate photons collected per pixel from exposure, f-number and quantum efficiency, model arrival as Poisson, and show SNR grows as the square root of photon count.

skills.name: Read noise, full-well capacity and dynamic range
skills.description: Compute sensor dynamic range in decibels and stops from full-well capacity and read noise, and predict when bright windows saturate a robot's view.

skills.name: Motion blur from exposure time and motion
skills.description: Compute blur length in pixels from object or head angular rate, exposure time and per-pixel angle, and set a maximum exposure for sharp images.

skills.name: Near-infrared light and silicon sensor response
skills.description: Explain why silicon sensors respond out to about 1000 nanometers, why color cameras use IR-cut filters, and trade-offs between 850 and 940 nanometer illumination.

skills.name: Laser and active triangulation range geometry
skills.description: Derive range from the baseline, focal length and spot position in an active triangulation sensor, and show depth error grows with range squared.

skills.name: Pulsed time-of-flight timing resolution
skills.description: Relate round-trip light travel time to distance, showing one nanosecond corresponds to fifteen centimeters, and derive range resolution from timing jitter.

skills.name: Diffuse versus specular returns in active sensing
skills.description: Explain Lambertian diffuse reflection, specular mirrors and retroreflectors, and predict weak or false returns from dark, shiny or glass targets.

skills.name: Sensor windows and IR-transmissive covers
skills.description: Estimate Fresnel reflection losses at a cover window, avoid internal reflections that blind depth sensors, and choose tinted plastics that pass near-infrared.

skills.name: Laser safety classes and eye hazard
skills.description: Interpret laser classes 1 through 4, explain why invisible near-infrared beams are hazardous to eyes, and check emitter labels for a robot used around people.

skills.name: Radiometric and photometric units
skills.description: Distinguish watts from lumens using the eye's luminous efficiency curve, and compute luminous flux from radiant power at a given wavelength.

skills.name: Luminous intensity, solid angle and illuminance
skills.description: Relate candela, lumens per steradian and lux, use solid angle to convert a beam's intensity to flux, and apply the inverse-square law for illuminance.

skills.name: Luminance of displays and surfaces
skills.description: Define luminance in candela per square meter, compute it for a diffuse lit surface, and compare a face display's nits with indoor and daylight conditions.

skills.name: How LEDs emit light: bandgap and wavelength
skills.description: Relate an LED's semiconductor bandgap to emission wavelength and forward voltage, and explain how white LEDs combine a blue die with phosphor.

skills.name: LED efficacy, droop and junction heating
skills.description: Estimate the fraction of LED power converted to heat, explain efficiency droop at high current, and predict brightness and color shift as the junction warms.

skills.name: PWM dimming, flicker and perceived brightness
skills.description: Explain why perceived brightness is nonlinear in duty cycle, apply gamma correction, and choose PWM frequencies that avoid visible flicker and camera banding.

skills.name: Diffusing LED light without hot spots
skills.description: Choose diffuser material, thickness and LED-to-diffuser spacing so discrete LEDs blend into an even glowing surface for eyes or a face panel.

skills.name: Work in the Linux shell
skills.description: Move around the filesystem, search with find and grep, edit files in a terminal editor, and use history and tab completion fluently while working on a robot computer.

skills.name: File permissions, ownership and groups
skills.description: Read and change permission bits, owners and group membership, use sudo deliberately, and grant a user access to serial and camera devices through groups like dialout and video.

skills.name: Environment variables and shell startup files
skills.description: Set, export and inspect environment variables, explain how PATH is searched, and decide what belongs in .bashrc versus a per-project setup script.

skills.name: Install and manage software with apt
skills.description: Install, upgrade, pin and remove packages with apt, add a signed third-party repository, and explain the difference between system packages and per-project dependencies.

skills.name: Write robust Bash scripts
skills.description: Write Bash scripts that parse arguments, quote variables safely, stop on errors with set -euo pipefail, and return meaningful exit codes for use in automation.

skills.name: Inspect and control processes and signals
skills.description: Use ps, top and pgrep to find processes, send SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGKILL appropriately, and explain how a program should shut down cleanly on a signal.

skills.name: Read kernel and service logs with dmesg and journalctl
skills.description: Use dmesg and journalctl to identify a newly plugged USB device, filter logs by unit and time, and spot driver errors or brownout resets.

skills.name: Give devices stable names with udev rules
skills.description: Write a udev rule that matches a USB serial adapter or camera by vendor, product and serial number, creates a fixed symlink, and sets its permissions.

skills.name: Remote access with SSH keys, scp and rsync
skills.description: Generate an SSH key pair, log in to a robot without passwords, use an ssh config file, and copy or synchronize code with scp and rsync.

skills.name: Run a robot program as a systemd service
skills.description: Write a systemd unit with restart policy, user, environment and dependencies so a robot stack starts at boot, and control it with systemctl.

skills.name: Track code with Git commits and branches
skills.description: Run a daily Git workflow on a robot project: inspect status and diffs, stage selectively, write clear commit messages, and create and switch feature branches.

skills.name: Exclude generated files with .gitignore
skills.description: Write .gitignore patterns that keep build, install, log, bag and virtual-environment folders out of the repository while keeping configuration and source tracked.

skills.name: Resolve merge conflicts and rebase a branch
skills.description: Merge or rebase a feature branch onto main, read conflict markers, resolve them correctly, and recover with stash, revert or reflog when something goes wrong.

skills.name: Open and review a pull request on GitHub
skills.description: Push a branch, open a pull request with a useful description, respond to review comments, and review someone else's change for correctness and clarity.

skills.name: Tag versions and publish releases
skills.description: Apply semantic versioning, create annotated tags, write release notes, and identify exactly which code version is running on a robot from its tag.

skills.name: Python virtual environments and pip
skills.description: Create a venv, install pinned dependencies with pip from a requirements file, and explain why isolating project environments prevents version conflicts on a shared robot computer.

skills.name: Python dataclasses, properties and special methods
skills.description: Write Python classes using dataclasses, properties and methods like __repr__ and __eq__ to model robot data such as joint states and poses.

skills.name: Inheritance, composition and abstract base classes
skills.description: Choose between inheritance and composition, and define an abstract base class that several concrete implementations, such as real and simulated drivers, must satisfy.

skills.name: Custom exceptions and context managers
skills.description: Define a hierarchy of custom exceptions, raise and catch them precisely, and use with-blocks and context managers to guarantee hardware connections are closed.

skills.name: Read and write CSV, JSON and YAML
skills.description: Load and save robot data and configuration in CSV, JSON and YAML with the standard libraries, validating fields and handling malformed files gracefully.

skills.name: Structure a Python package with pyproject.toml
skills.description: Organize code into an installable package with pyproject.toml, entry points and relative imports, and install it in editable mode for development.

skills.name: Type hints and static checking with mypy
skills.description: Annotate functions and classes with type hints including Optional, generics and Protocols, and run mypy to catch interface mistakes before running code.

skills.name: Array computing with NumPy
skills.description: Create, index, slice and reshape NumPy arrays, choose dtypes, and replace Python loops with array operations for sensor and joint data.

skills.name: NumPy broadcasting and vectorized math
skills.description: Predict the result shape of broadcast operations, apply operations across many points or timesteps at once, and avoid silent shape bugs.

skills.name: Linear algebra with numpy.linalg
skills.description: Multiply matrices with the @ operator, solve linear systems, compute least-squares fits, norms and SVDs, and check numerical results against expectations.

skills.name: Rotations and rigid transforms in Python code
skills.description: Build, compose and invert 4x4 homogeneous transforms with NumPy and convert between rotation matrices, quaternions and Euler angles using scipy.spatial.transform.

skills.name: Plot robot data with matplotlib
skills.description: Plot time series, subplots and XY trajectories with labeled axes, units and legends so commanded and measured signals can be compared visually.

skills.name: SciPy optimize, interpolate and integrate
skills.description: Use scipy.optimize to fit or minimize, scipy.interpolate to resample trajectories, and solve_ivp to integrate a simple dynamic model.

skills.name: Filter sensor signals with scipy.signal
skills.description: Design low-pass and Butterworth filters, apply them causally and zero-phase to logged signals, and compare the lag each introduces.

skills.name: Asynchronous Python with asyncio
skills.description: Write coroutines with async and await, run concurrent tasks, apply timeouts and cancellation, and know when asyncio suits network and I/O-bound robot code.

skills.name: Compile and link C++ with headers
skills.description: Split C++ code into headers and source files with include guards, compile and link with g++, and interpret common compiler and linker errors.

skills.name: C++ references, pointers and const
skills.description: Choose between pass-by-value, reference, const reference and pointer, and apply const correctness to function parameters and member functions.

skills.name: C++ classes, references and the build
skills.description: Write C++ classes with constructors, member initializer lists and access control, organized into header and source files that build cleanly.

skills.name: Build C++ projects with CMake
skills.description: Write a CMakeLists.txt with targets, include directories, find_package and target_link_libraries, and build out of source in Debug and Release modes.

skills.name: STL containers
skills.description: Choose and use std::vector, std::array, std::map and std::unordered_map, iterate with range-for, and reason about reallocation and lookup cost.

skills.name: RAII and object lifetime
skills.description: Tie resource ownership such as file handles, sockets and device connections to object lifetime, and apply the rule of zero and rule of five.

skills.name: Smart pointers and ownership
skills.description: Use unique_ptr, shared_ptr and weak_ptr to express ownership, avoid raw new and delete, and break reference cycles.

skills.name: C++ templates basics
skills.description: Write and use simple function and class templates, read template error messages, and understand why header-only template code is common.

skills.name: Virtual functions and interface classes
skills.description: Define abstract interface classes with pure virtual functions, override them safely, and hold implementations through base-class smart pointers, as plugin systems require.

skills.name: Linear algebra with Eigen
skills.description: Use Eigen fixed and dynamic vectors and matrices, solve linear systems and least squares, and avoid aliasing and alignment pitfalls.

skills.name: Eigen geometry: quaternions and Isometry3d
skills.description: Represent poses with Eigen Isometry3d, Quaterniond and AngleAxisd, compose and invert them, and convert to and from ROS message types.

skills.name: Find memory bugs with gdb and sanitizers
skills.description: Debug crashes in C++ with gdb backtraces, and detect use-after-free, leaks and undefined behavior with AddressSanitizer and UBSan builds.

skills.name: Install ROS 2 and source its environment
skills.description: Install a ROS 2 LTS distribution matched to the Ubuntu release, source setup files correctly, and verify the installation with demo nodes.

skills.name: The ROS 2 computation graph
skills.description: Explain nodes, topics, services, actions and parameters, and choose which communication pattern fits a given robot data flow or command.

skills.name: Inspect a running system with ros2 CLI tools
skills.description: Use ros2 node, topic, service and param commands plus rqt_graph to list, echo, measure rates of and introspect a live ROS 2 system.

skills.name: ROS 2 workspaces and colcon builds
skills.description: Create a workspace, build selected packages with colcon, use symlink installs, and explain underlays and overlays when sourcing several workspaces.

skills.name: Create ROS 2 Python and C++ packages
skills.description: Create ament_python and ament_cmake packages, declare dependencies in package.xml, register executables, and install launch and config files.

skills.name: Write a ROS 2 node with timers in rclpy
skills.description: Write an rclpy node class with a timer callback, spin it, and shut it down cleanly on Ctrl-C.

skills.name: Write a ROS 2 publisher and subscriber
skills.description: Write nodes that publish and subscribe to topics, process incoming messages in callbacks, and verify data flow with ros2 topic tools.

skills.name: Standard ROS 2 message types and headers
skills.description: Use std_msgs, geometry_msgs and sensor_msgs correctly, fill headers with stamps and frame ids, and respect ROS unit and sign conventions.

skills.name: Write ROS 2 services and clients
skills.description: Implement a service server and client, call services asynchronously without deadlocking a node, and handle timeouts and unavailable servers.

skills.name: ROS 2 parameters and YAML configuration
skills.description: Declare typed parameters with defaults, load them from YAML, change them at runtime, and validate changes in a parameter callback.

skills.name: Write Python launch files
skills.description: Write launch files that start several nodes with parameters, arguments, remappings and conditional logic, and include other launch files.

skills.name: Write ROS 2 nodes in C++ with rclcpp
skills.description: Write rclcpp nodes with publishers, subscriptions, timers and parameters, and build them with ament_cmake for lower latency than Python.

skills.name: Define custom ROS 2 messages, services and actions
skills.description: Write .msg, .srv and .action definitions in an interface package, build them, and use the generated types from Python and C++ nodes.

skills.name: Write ROS 2 action servers and clients
skills.description: Implement a long-running action with goals, periodic feedback, results and cancellation, and write a client that monitors and preempts it.

skills.name: ROS 2 quality of service settings
skills.description: Choose reliability, durability, history depth and deadline policies for sensor, command and latched data, and diagnose incompatible QoS between endpoints.

skills.name: ROS time, simulated time and timestamps
skills.description: Distinguish wall, steady and ROS time, enable use_sim_time, and stamp and compare messages correctly when data comes from several sources.

skills.name: Executors and callback groups
skills.description: Explain single and multithreaded executors, assign callbacks to mutually exclusive or reentrant groups, and avoid blocking that starves other callbacks.

skills.name: Lifecycle managed nodes
skills.description: Implement a lifecycle node with configure, activate, deactivate and cleanup transitions, and drive transitions from a manager for orderly startup and shutdown.

skills.name: Namespaces and remapping for repeated subsystems
skills.description: Run two copies of the same driver or controller, such as left and right arms, using namespaces, remapping and frame prefixes without collisions.

skills.name: Debug a ROS 2 system
skills.description: Diagnose missing data, wrong rates and crashed nodes using rqt_console, log levels, ros2 doctor, topic hz and delay, and node introspection.

skills.name: Manage dependencies with rosdep and vcstool
skills.description: Resolve system dependencies with rosdep and assemble a multi-repository workspace reproducibly from a .repos file with vcstool.

skills.name: Broadcast and look up transforms with tf2
skills.description: Broadcast static and dynamic transforms, look up the transform between two frames at a given time, and handle lookup timeouts and extrapolation errors.

skills.name: Standard robot frame conventions
skills.description: Apply REP 103 axis and unit conventions and the REP 105 map, odom and base_link frame hierarchy to keep a robot's transform tree consistent.

skills.name: Visualize robot state in RViz
skills.description: Configure RViz to display the robot model, TF frames, sensor data and custom markers, and save configurations for repeatable debugging sessions.

skills.name: Record and replay robot data with rosbag
skills.description: Record selected topics with ros2 bag, inspect bag metadata, replay with simulated clock and rate control, and choose storage formats and compression.

skills.name: Analyze bag files in Python
skills.description: Read bag files programmatically, extract messages into NumPy arrays aligned by timestamp, and plot or compute metrics from them.

skills.name: Write a URDF robot description
skills.description: Describe links and revolute, prismatic, continuous and fixed joints in URDF with correct origins, axes and limits for a simple arm.

skills.name: Parameterize robot descriptions with xacro
skills.description: Use xacro properties, math expressions, macros and includes to build reusable limb descriptions and generate mirrored left and right arms.

skills.name: Inertial parameters in robot descriptions
skills.description: Specify link mass, center of mass and inertia tensor from CAD or primitives, and check values for physical plausibility before simulation.

skills.name: Visual and collision geometry
skills.description: Separate detailed visual meshes from simplified collision geometry, use primitives or convex decompositions, and check scale and origin errors.

skills.name: Export a CAD assembly to a robot description
skills.description: Export link meshes and joint frames from a CAD assembly into a URDF or xacro, matching joint origins, axes and mass properties to the design.

skills.name: robot_state_publisher and joint states
skills.description: Publish joint_states and use robot_state_publisher to turn the URDF into a live TF tree, verifying it with joint_state_publisher_gui and RViz.

skills.name: ros2_control architecture
skills.description: Explain the controller manager, resource manager, hardware components and command and state interfaces, and how they are declared in the URDF.

skills.name: Configure and switch ros2_control controllers
skills.description: Configure joint_state_broadcaster, forward command and joint trajectory controllers in YAML, then load, activate and switch them, first against mock hardware.

skills.name: Write a ros2_control hardware interface
skills.description: Implement a SystemInterface plugin that exports state and command interfaces and reads and writes real actuators, such as smart servos, each control cycle.

skills.name: Command arm motions through a trajectory controller
skills.description: Send a FollowJointTrajectory goal with timed waypoints, monitor tolerances and feedback, and interpret aborted goals.

skills.name: Configure diff_drive_controller for a wheeled base
skills.description: Configure wheel separation, radius, limits and odometry publishing in diff_drive_controller and verify that velocity commands move the base as expected.

skills.name: Write a custom ros2_control controller
skills.description: Implement a ControllerInterface plugin that claims interfaces, runs a control law in update(), and exposes parameters and reference topics safely.

skills.name: Simulate a robot model in Gazebo or MuJoCo
skills.description: Load a robot description into Gazebo or MuJoCo, run the simulation, apply joint commands, and observe that motion and gravity behave plausibly.

skills.name: Physics engine timestep, solver and contact settings
skills.description: Tune simulation timestep, solver iterations, friction and contact stiffness and damping, and recognize instability, jitter and interpenetration symptoms.

skills.name: Bridge Gazebo and ROS 2
skills.description: Spawn a robot into Gazebo from a launch file, bridge topics with ros_gz_bridge, and run nodes on the simulation clock.

skills.name: Drive simulated joints with gz_ros2_control
skills.description: Replace real hardware with the Gazebo ros2_control plugin so the same controllers and configuration run in simulation and on the robot.

skills.name: Describe a robot in MuJoCo MJCF
skills.description: Write or convert an MJCF model with bodies, joints, actuators, geoms and defaults, and compare its kinematics and inertias with the URDF.

skills.name: Control a MuJoCo simulation from Python
skills.description: Load an MJCF model with the mujoco Python bindings, step it at a fixed rate, read sensor data, apply controls and render or record the result.

skills.name: Simulate cameras, depth, lidar and IMU
skills.description: Add simulated cameras, depth sensors, lidar and IMUs to a model, configure their rates and noise, and publish them as ROS 2 topics.

skills.name: Isaac Sim and GPU-parallel simulation
skills.description: Explain what Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab offer, including USD scenes, photorealistic sensors and thousands of parallel environments, and when their hardware cost is justified.

skills.name: The sim-to-real gap
skills.description: Identify mismatches in dynamics, friction, latency and sensing between simulation and hardware, and reduce them with system identification and domain randomization.

skills.name: Decompose robot software into modules
skills.description: Split a robot application into modules with single responsibilities and explicit interfaces, and draw the data flow between them.

skills.name: Hardware abstraction and mock drivers
skills.description: Design a driver interface with real, simulated and mock implementations so higher-level code and tests run unchanged without the hardware.

skills.name: Behavior tree concepts
skills.description: Explain sequences, fallbacks, parallels, decorators, the tick model and blackboards, and compare behavior trees with finite-state machines for robot tasks.

skills.name: Build a behavior tree with BehaviorTree.CPP or py_trees
skills.description: Implement action and condition nodes that wrap ROS 2 actions and services, compose them into a tree, and monitor its execution live.

skills.name: Design fault handling and recovery behaviors
skills.description: Classify recoverable and unrecoverable faults, design retries, timeouts and safe fallback behaviors, and make every failure visible to the operator.

skills.name: Design a robot skill API for a task layer
skills.description: Expose robot capabilities such as move to, pick and say as well-defined, validated actions with preconditions and results that a planner or language model can call.

skills.name: Python threads, the GIL and queues
skills.description: Run background I/O in Python threads, pass data safely through queue.Queue, and explain how the global interpreter lock limits CPU-bound parallelism.

skills.name: C++ threads, mutexes and condition variables
skills.description: Start std::threads, protect shared data with mutex and lock_guard, signal with condition_variable, and join threads cleanly on shutdown.

skills.name: Atomics and lock-free queues for control loops
skills.description: Use std::atomic and a single-producer single-consumer ring buffer to pass data into a real-time loop without blocking on locks.

skills.name: Thread-safe ROS 2 callbacks
skills.description: Identify shared state touched by callbacks in a multithreaded executor and protect it with locks or callback groups so no races occur.

skills.name: Real-time Linux for control loops
skills.description: Configure a PREEMPT_RT kernel, thread priorities, memory locking and CPU isolation, and measure the resulting worst-case loop jitter.

skills.name: Profile Python code
skills.description: Find hot spots with cProfile and py-spy, read the output, and confirm that an optimization actually reduced time in the measured path.

skills.name: Profile C++ code with perf and flame graphs
skills.description: Build with symbols and optimization, sample a running program with perf, read a flame graph, and relate hot spots to cache and allocation behavior.

skills.name: Measure end-to-end latency in a ROS 2 pipeline
skills.description: Measure latency from sensor capture to actuator command using timestamps and tracing, and attribute delay to transport, queuing and computation.

skills.name: DDS discovery, domain IDs and RMW choice
skills.description: Explain how DDS participants discover each other, isolate robots with ROS_DOMAIN_ID, and choose and switch RMW implementations.

skills.name: Run ROS 2 across robot and laptop
skills.description: Configure network addresses, hostnames, firewall and DDS settings so nodes on the robot and a development laptop communicate reliably.

skills.name: Diagnose Wi-Fi latency and bandwidth limits
skills.description: Measure round-trip time, jitter and throughput with ping and iperf, and reduce wireless load by compressing images and throttling topics.

skills.name: Tune DDS for constrained networks
skills.description: Use a discovery server, localhost-only mode, shared memory transport and topic filtering to keep high-rate data on the robot off the wireless link.

skills.name: Lint and format code automatically
skills.description: Enforce consistent style with ruff, black and clang-format, catch common mistakes with linters, and run them automatically with pre-commit hooks.

skills.name: Write tests with pytest
skills.description: Write pytest tests with fixtures, parametrization and floating-point tolerances, and measure coverage for robot math and logic modules.

skills.name: Unit-test C++ with GoogleTest
skills.description: Write GoogleTest cases and fixtures, register them with CTest through CMake, and compare floating-point results with appropriate tolerances.

skills.name: Test with fakes and mocks of hardware
skills.description: Replace serial ports, motors and sensors with fakes or unittest.mock objects to test driver and control logic deterministically.

skills.name: Test ROS 2 packages with colcon test
skills.description: Add Python and C++ tests to ROS 2 packages, run them with colcon test, and read colcon test-result output.

skills.name: Integration tests with launch_testing
skills.description: Write launch_testing tests that start several nodes, publish inputs, assert on outputs within timeouts and check clean process exit.

skills.name: Regression tests from recorded bags
skills.description: Replay recorded bag data through a node in a test and compare outputs with stored expected results to catch behavior changes.

skills.name: Headless simulation scenario tests
skills.description: Run a simulator headless in tests, script scenarios with pass and fail criteria such as reach a pose without collision, and report results automatically.

skills.name: Continuous integration with GitHub Actions
skills.description: Write a GitHub Actions workflow that installs dependencies, lints, and runs tests on every pull request, and read failing job logs.

skills.name: Build and test a ROS 2 workspace in CI
skills.description: Configure CI to build a ROS 2 workspace with rosdep and colcon, run unit and launch tests, and cache dependencies to keep runs fast.

skills.name: Python logging module
skills.description: Configure loggers, levels, handlers and formatters, log with context instead of print, and rotate log files on a long-running robot.

skills.name: Publish health with ROS 2 diagnostics
skills.description: Report component health with diagnostic_updater, aggregate it with diagnostic_aggregator, and define OK, warning and error thresholds for voltages, temperatures and rates.

skills.name: Plot live and logged signals with PlotJuggler
skills.description: Stream live topics or load bags into PlotJuggler, arrange synchronized plots, and apply derivative and custom transforms to inspect control behavior.

skills.name: Build dashboards with Foxglove
skills.description: Connect Foxglove to a robot through foxglove_bridge, build layouts with 3D, image, plot and log panels, and share them for remote debugging.

skills.name: Structured telemetry and metrics history
skills.description: Collect timestamped metrics such as loop rates, temperatures and task outcomes into a time-series store, and query trends across many runs.

skills.name: Build a web control panel for the robot
skills.description: Build a simple browser interface that shows robot status and sends safe commands through rosbridge or an async Python web server.

skills.name: Build and run Docker containers
skills.description: Write a Dockerfile, build and tag images, run containers with volumes and ports, and explain layers and caching for fast rebuilds.

skills.name: Containerize a ROS 2 robot stack
skills.description: Run a ROS 2 workspace in containers with host networking, device and GPU access, and compose multiple services with docker compose.

skills.name: Keep secrets and keys out of code
skills.description: Store API keys and credentials in environment files or a secrets store, exclude them from Git, and rotate a key that leaked.

skills.name: Manage per-robot configuration
skills.description: Separate code from per-robot parameters and calibration files, version them, and load the correct set for each robot and environment.

skills.name: Deploy, update and roll back robot software
skills.description: Ship a tagged release to the robot, start it as a service, verify it, and roll back to the previous version quickly when it misbehaves.

skills.name: Write a robot bringup package
skills.description: Create a bringup package whose launch files start drivers, controllers, description, perception and diagnostics in order with the right configuration for each robot.

skills.name: Integrate the humanoid software stack
skills.description: Assemble drivers, controllers, perception, behavior trees and dialogue into one reproducible, monitored deployment that meets the humanoid's latency and reliability budgets.

skills.name: Elicit stakeholder needs for a protocol droid
skills.description: Interview users, owners and bystanders to list what a helpful talking humanoid must do, and record each need with its source and priority.

skills.name: Translate needs into shall statements
skills.description: Rewrite a vague stakeholder need such as 'greets visitors politely' into one or more singular shall statements with a subject, action and condition.

skills.name: Write measurable robot requirements
skills.description: Write humanoid requirements with numeric thresholds, units, tolerances and test conditions, such as response latency, reach envelope or payload, so that pass or fail is unambiguous.

skills.name: Assign a verification method to each requirement
skills.description: Choose test, analysis, inspection or demonstration as the verification method for each requirement and justify the choice from cost, risk and observability.

skills.name: Build a requirements traceability matrix
skills.description: Link every stakeholder need to its requirements, design elements and verification evidence in a matrix, and find orphan requirements and unverified needs.

skills.name: Write a concept of operations for a protocol droid
skills.description: Describe who uses the droid, where, when and how, including a typical day, staffing, charging and failure handling, as a narrative that anchors all requirements.

skills.name: Write use cases and operational scenarios
skills.description: Write use cases with actors, preconditions, main flow, alternate flows and failure flows for tasks such as greeting a visitor or fetching an item.

skills.name: Specify the operating environment and design envelope
skills.description: Specify floor types, slopes, lighting, ambient noise, crowd density, temperature and network availability the droid must tolerate, with quantified bounds.

skills.name: Define robot operating modes and transitions
skills.description: Define modes such as off, standby, teleoperated, autonomous, charging, maintenance and fault, with allowed transitions, entry conditions and who may command each change.

skills.name: Decompose robot functions into a function tree
skills.description: Break the top-level mission into a hierarchy of functions such as perceive, decide, move, manipulate and communicate down to testable leaf functions.

skills.name: Map functions to physical subsystems
skills.description: Allocate each leaf function to hardware or software subsystems, and judge alternative allocations by coupling, interface count and testability.

skills.name: Allocate and derive subsystem requirements
skills.description: Allocate system requirements to subsystems and derive child requirements, such as splitting an end-to-end latency limit between perception, planning and actuation.

skills.name: Draw a system block diagram
skills.description: Draw a robot block diagram that distinguishes power, data and mechanical connections between subsystems, labeled with voltages, buses and load paths.

skills.name: Map data flow and message rates
skills.description: Draw the data flow between sensors, compute nodes and actuators with topic names, message sizes and rates, and compute required bandwidth on each link.

skills.name: Build an N-squared interface matrix
skills.description: Build an N-squared matrix of subsystem interfaces to enumerate every mechanical, electrical, data and thermal interaction and spot missing or unexpected couplings.

skills.name: Write an interface control document
skills.description: Write an interface control document specifying connector pinouts, voltages, message formats, rates, frames, mounting features and ownership for one subsystem boundary.

skills.name: Plan the robot's internal network topology
skills.description: Choose how CAN, Ethernet, USB and serial links connect controllers and computers, assigning addresses and checking bus load and single points of failure.

skills.name: Partition compute across MCUs, SBC and GPU
skills.description: Decide which functions run on microcontrollers, a Linux computer or an accelerator based on timing determinism, compute load, power and failure isolation.

skills.name: Define the architecture of a wheeled humanoid droid
skills.description: Produce the complete subsystem breakdown, block diagram and interface list for a wheeled humanoid with torso, arms, hands, head, speech and base.

skills.name: Define weighted criteria for a trade study
skills.description: Derive trade-study criteria from requirements, assign normalized weights, and define scoring scales so that alternatives can be compared consistently.

skills.name: Run a weighted trade study
skills.description: Score design alternatives, such as servo versus custom BLDC joints, against weighted criteria and document the recommended option and its rationale.

skills.name: Apply maturity-based design margins
skills.description: Set contingency margins on budgeted quantities according to design maturity, from estimated through measured, and shrink them as data improves.

skills.name: Build a mass and center-of-mass budget
skills.description: Tabulate subsystem masses and positions with margins to compute total mass and center of mass, and compare them with stability and actuator limits.

skills.name: Build a compute and memory budget
skills.description: Estimate CPU, GPU and memory use for each software node and model, compare with platform capacity and headroom targets, and verify by profiling.

skills.name: Build an end-to-end latency budget
skills.description: Allocate latency along a chain such as hearing a question to starting a spoken reply, sum stage delays and jitter, and identify the dominant contributors.

skills.name: Build a thermal budget for enclosed electronics
skills.description: Sum heat dissipation inside each enclosure, estimate temperature rise through thermal resistances, and check component and surface temperature limits.

skills.name: Mass, power, compute and latency budgets
skills.description: Maintain a consolidated budget of mass, power, energy, compute, latency and heat for the humanoid, with margins and owners, and flag any exceeded allocation.

skills.name: Assign part numbers and revisions
skills.description: Apply a part numbering and revision scheme so each drawing, printed part, harness and board has a unique identity and a clear change history.

skills.name: Build an indented bill of materials
skills.description: Build an indented bill of materials from a CAD assembly with quantities, part numbers, suppliers, unit costs and make-or-buy status.

skills.name: Track as-designed versus as-built configuration
skills.description: Record serial numbers, revisions and modifications of each built unit so the as-built robot can be compared with the released as-designed configuration.

skills.name: Run engineering change control
skills.description: Raise and evaluate an engineering change request, assess impacts on interfaces, requirements, cost and schedule, and release the approved change.

skills.name: Record hardware, firmware and software compatibility
skills.description: Maintain a version manifest tying firmware builds, software releases, calibration files and hardware revisions together so any configuration can be reproduced.

skills.name: Select suppliers and second sources
skills.description: Choose suppliers for key components using datasheets, availability, price breaks and support, and identify second sources for single-source risks.

skills.name: Plan around lead times and long-lead items
skills.description: Identify long-lead components, estimate order-to-delivery times, and schedule purchases so integration is not blocked by missing parts.

skills.name: Estimate and budget build cost
skills.description: Roll up a cost estimate from the bill of materials including tooling, spares, shipping and contingency, and compare it with the available budget.

skills.name: Keep an engineering build log
skills.description: Keep dated build-log entries recording what was built, measured, changed and observed, with photos and values, so work can be reproduced and debugged.

skills.name: Draw a robot-level wiring diagram
skills.description: Draw a wiring diagram with connector designators, pinouts, wire gauges, colors, labels, fuses and routing that a second person could build from.

skills.name: Write assembly procedures with checks
skills.description: Write step-by-step assembly instructions with exploded views, torque values, adhesive notes and inspection checkpoints for a robot module.

skills.name: Run a design review
skills.description: Prepare and run a preliminary or critical design review with a checklist covering requirements, interfaces, risks and open actions, and record decisions.

skills.name: Write an operator manual
skills.description: Write an operator manual covering startup, shutdown, modes, charging, emergency stopping, fault messages and routine checks for nontechnical users.

skills.name: Write a test plan
skills.description: Write a test plan listing objectives, requirements covered, setup, equipment, sequence, pass criteria and safety precautions for a robot subsystem.

skills.name: Write a step-by-step test procedure
skills.description: Write a repeatable test procedure with numbered steps, expected readings and record fields so another person obtains comparable results.

skills.name: Write a test report
skills.description: Write a test report that presents measured data, deviations from procedure, anomalies and a pass or fail verdict traced to each requirement.

skills.name: Design a test fixture or jig
skills.description: Design a fixture that holds a subsystem and applies known loads or motions so a test is repeatable and safe, such as a joint load rig.

skills.name: Run subsystem acceptance tests
skills.description: Define and run acceptance tests that a subsystem must pass before integration, recording results against its interface control document and requirements.

skills.name: Choose an integration order
skills.description: Order subsystem integration steps from a dependency graph so each step adds one unknown, choosing between bottom-up and thread-based sequences.

skills.name: Write a first power-on bring-up checklist
skills.description: Write and follow a bring-up checklist using current-limited supplies, continuity checks, e-stop tests and staged enabling of actuators before full operation.

skills.name: Incremental integration and bring-up plan
skills.description: Produce an integration plan sequencing subsystem bring-up, tests at each step, entry and exit criteria, fallbacks and resources for an entire robot.

skills.name: Test a controller with hardware in the loop
skills.description: Connect real controller firmware or hardware to a simulated plant to test control and fault logic before risking the physical robot.

skills.name: Maintain a hardware and software regression suite
skills.description: Maintain a set of quick tests rerun after every change to catch regressions in motion, sensing and behavior, and log results over time.

skills.name: Monitor integrated robot health telemetry
skills.description: Publish and visualize health signals such as temperatures, currents, voltages, loop timing and error counts, with thresholds that raise warnings.

skills.name: Track issues with severity and closure
skills.description: Log defects with reproduction steps, severity, owner and status, and close them only with evidence that the fix was verified.

skills.name: Isolate a fault across subsystems
skills.description: Isolate a system-level fault by splitting the signal chain at interfaces and testing each half, narrowing the cause to one subsystem efficiently.

skills.name: Reconstruct a failure from synchronized logs
skills.description: Align recorded logs from several subsystems on a common time base to reconstruct the sequence of events leading to a failure.

skills.name: Perform root cause analysis
skills.description: Use five-whys and fishbone methods to move from symptom to root cause, then define a corrective action and a check that it worked.

skills.name: Diagnose intermittent faults
skills.description: Diagnose intermittent faults from loose connectors, interference, timing races or thermal effects using stress tests, logging and controlled variation.

skills.name: Failure rate, MTBF and the reliability function
skills.description: Compute reliability over a mission time from a constant failure rate, and relate failure rate, MTBF and probability of surviving a given duration.

skills.name: Reliability of series and redundant systems
skills.description: Calculate system reliability from component reliabilities for series chains and parallel redundancy, and identify the weakest elements.

skills.name: Failure modes and effects analysis
skills.description: Perform a failure modes and effects analysis listing each component failure mode, its effects, causes and detection, and rank them by severity, occurrence and detection.

skills.name: Build and evaluate a fault tree
skills.description: Build a fault tree for an undesired top event such as an uncommanded arm motion and compute its probability from basic event probabilities.

skills.name: Plan burn-in to remove early failures
skills.description: Use the bathtub curve to plan a burn-in period for new actuators and electronics that exposes early-life failures before the robot is used with people.

skills.name: Confidence bounds on task success rate
skills.description: Compute a confidence interval for a task success rate from repeated trials and determine how many trials are needed to claim a target rate.

skills.name: Run repeat-run endurance tests
skills.description: Run a task many times under controlled conditions, record every outcome and failure, and report success rate with confidence bounds and failure modes.

skills.name: Track cycle counts and component wear
skills.description: Track joint cycles, cable flexes, operating hours and measured backlash per component to predict wear-out and schedule replacement.

skills.name: Write a preventive maintenance plan
skills.description: Write a preventive maintenance schedule of inspections, lubrication, recalibration and replacements derived from wear data and the FMEA.

skills.name: Plan spares and swappable modules
skills.description: Choose which modules to stock as spares from failure likelihood, repair time and lead time, and design for quick module swaps.

skills.name: Identify robot hazards systematically
skills.description: Identify mechanical, electrical, thermal, behavioral and environmental hazards across every use case and lifecycle phase from assembly to disposal.

skills.name: Estimate risk with a severity-probability matrix
skills.description: Rate each hazard's severity and likelihood on defined scales, place it on a risk matrix, and decide whether the risk is acceptable.

skills.name: Apply the risk reduction hierarchy
skills.description: Reduce risk in priority order: inherently safe design, then safeguards and protective devices, then warnings and training, and justify each choice.

skills.name: Specify robot safety functions
skills.description: Specify safety functions such as protective stop, speed limiting, zone limiting and torque limiting, each with trigger, response, response time and safe state.

skills.name: Stop categories and safe torque off
skills.description: Distinguish stop categories 0, 1 and 2 and safe torque off, and select which applies to each joint given gravity loads and brakes.

skills.name: Define safe states for each failure
skills.description: Define what each subsystem does on fault, power loss or communication loss, such as braking, holding or going limp, and check the result is actually safe.

skills.name: Review an emergency stop design
skills.description: Review an emergency stop circuit for independence from software, single-fault behavior, reset logic, reachability and periodic testing.

skills.name: Identify and mitigate pinch and crush points
skills.description: Find pinch, crush and shear points in arms, hands, neck and torso joints and mitigate them with gaps, covers, torque limits or geometry changes.

skills.name: Assess tip-over hazard of a tall mobile robot
skills.description: Compute tip-over margins of a tall wheeled humanoid during acceleration, braking, slopes and arm extension, and set motion limits to keep it stable.

skills.name: Plan lithium battery fire safety
skills.description: Plan safe charging, storage, transport and damaged-cell handling for lithium packs, and define the response to swelling, smoke or thermal runaway.

skills.name: Review electrical safety of a robot
skills.description: Review fusing, wire ratings, insulation, strain relief, touch-accessible voltages and grounding against the wiring diagram, and record nonconformities.

skills.name: Navigate type A, B and C safety standards
skills.description: Explain how basic, group and product safety standards relate and locate which ones apply to a service humanoid robot.

skills.name: ISO 12100 risk assessment process
skills.description: Apply the ISO 12100 sequence of determining limits, identifying hazards, estimating and evaluating risk, and reducing it iteratively, for a robot.

skills.name: ISO 10218 industrial robot safety concepts
skills.description: Explain ISO 10218 concepts such as protective stops, reduced speed, enabling devices and safeguarded spaces, and which transfer to a service robot.

skills.name: ISO/TS 15066 collaborative operation
skills.description: Explain the four collaborative operation modes and body-region contact limits of ISO/TS 15066, and when each mode suits a human-facing robot.

skills.name: ISO 13482 personal care robot concepts
skills.description: Explain how ISO 13482 classifies personal care robots and the hazards it emphasizes, such as instability, contact and autonomous behavior errors.

skills.name: Functional safety: IEC 61508 SIL and ISO 13849 PL
skills.description: Explain safety integrity levels and performance levels, how architecture, diagnostics and failure rates determine them, and why software alone rarely suffices.

skills.name: Speed and separation monitoring
skills.description: Compute the protective separation distance from human speed, robot speed, reaction time and stopping distance, and set speed limits for detected people.

skills.name: Power and force limiting
skills.description: Estimate contact force and transferred energy from effective mass and speed, and set joint speed and torque limits to stay below body-region thresholds.

skills.name: Measure collision forces on a robot
skills.description: Measure peak and quasi-static contact forces with a force gauge or instrumented target and compare them with allowed limits for each body region.

skills.name: Bound autonomous behavior with a safety supervisor
skills.description: Design a supervisor, independent of AI planners, that enforces speed, force, zone and mode limits on every commanded action and can veto unsafe commands.

skills.name: Robot risk assessment
skills.description: Produce a full risk assessment for a human-facing robot listing hazards, risk estimates, chosen measures and residual risk, following the ISO 12100 process.

skills.name: Validate safety functions by test
skills.description: Verify each safety function by test, such as measuring e-stop stopping time and distance and confirming safe states under injected faults, and record evidence.

skills.name: Threat-model a networked robot
skills.description: Identify assets, entry points and attackers for a networked robot and enumerate threats such as spoofed commands, data theft and denial of service.

skills.name: Harden robot network services
skills.description: Close unused ports, use key-based SSH, change default credentials, enable a firewall and restrict middleware discovery to trusted hosts.

skills.name: Deploy signed updates with rollback
skills.description: Deploy software and firmware updates that are authenticated, staged and reversible, so a failed or tampered update cannot leave the robot unsafe.

skills.name: Secure remote command and teleoperation
skills.description: Authenticate remote operators, authorize which commands they may send, and make the robot stop safely when the remote link drops or lags.

skills.name: Review privacy of cameras and microphones
skills.description: Assess what audio, video and personal data the droid captures, stores and sends, and apply minimization, retention limits, local processing and consent.

skills.name: Review ethics of a humanlike social robot
skills.description: Review risks of deception, overtrust, emotional dependence, vulnerable users and unclear AI disclosure, and decide design measures for each.

skills.name: Build a work breakdown structure
skills.description: Decompose the robot project into deliverable-oriented work packages that cover all hardware, software, testing and documentation work.

skills.name: Define milestones with entry and exit criteria
skills.description: Define project milestones with clear demonstrable exit criteria tied to requirements and tests, rather than effort spent.

skills.name: Build a schedule and find the critical path
skills.description: Build a dependency-based schedule with durations and lead times, compute the critical path and slack, and identify which delays move the end date.

skills.name: Track actual versus planned cost
skills.description: Track actual spending against the cost budget by work package, forecast the cost at completion, and flag overruns early.

skills.name: Maintain a project risk register
skills.description: Keep a register of technical, schedule and supply risks with likelihood, impact, owner, mitigation and trigger, and review it at each milestone.

skills.name: Control scope and descope deliberately
skills.description: Evaluate proposed feature additions against schedule and budget, define a minimum viable demonstration, and descope features with documented reasoning.

skills.name: Review a design for manufacture and assembly
skills.description: Review parts and assemblies for part count, process suitability, fastener commonality, tolerance needs and assembly access, and propose simplifications.

skills.name: Reduce cost through value engineering
skills.description: Find cost drivers in the bill of materials, compare should-cost estimates with quotes, and redesign or resource parts without breaking requirements.

skills.name: Design for serviceability
skills.description: Arrange modules, connectors and fasteners so common repairs and replacements are fast, safe and need few tools, and measure swap time.

skills.name: Plan a field trial
skills.description: Plan a trial in a real setting with protocol, metrics, observers, safety supervision, participant briefing, stop rules and data handling.

skills.name: Measure usability and user satisfaction
skills.description: Measure task success, completion time, interventions and questionnaire scores such as SUS, and summarize them with appropriate statistics.

skills.name: Report incidents and near misses
skills.description: Record incidents and near misses during trials with conditions, logs and immediate actions, and feed them back into the risk assessment.

skills.name: Run user acceptance testing
skills.description: Run acceptance tests with intended users against criteria traced to stakeholder needs and decide whether the robot is accepted, conditionally accepted or rejected.

skills.name: Integrate two arms on a torso
skills.description: Mount two arms on a torso with shared power and communication, a common base frame, mass checks and inter-arm collision limits, and verify each arm in place.

skills.name: Integrate hands at the wrists
skills.description: Integrate hands onto both arms, routing cables or tendons through the wrists, defining the wrist interface, and verifying grasp function after mounting.

skills.name: Integrate head and neck with cameras and microphones
skills.description: Integrate an actuated neck and sensor head, calibrate cameras and microphones to the torso frame, and verify gaze pointing accuracy.

skills.name: Integrate the expressive face into the head
skills.description: Integrate a face display or actuated features into the head, checking brightness, viewing angle, heat, cable routing and synchronization with speech.

skills.name: Integrate the speech pipeline on the robot
skills.description: Run microphones, speech recognition, dialogue and speech synthesis on the robot, handling motor self-noise, echo, barge-in and the end-to-end latency budget.

skills.name: Bring up coordinated upper-body control
skills.description: Bring up coordinated control of torso, both arms and neck with self-collision avoidance and joint limits, and verify combined motions at reduced speed.

skills.name: Mount the upper body on the wheeled base
skills.description: Mount the humanoid upper body on a wheeled base, merge power and networks, update stability limits, and verify driving with the upper body powered.

skills.name: Verify full-system power and runtime
skills.description: Power the complete humanoid through its distribution system, measure current under representative tasks, and verify runtime, brownout behavior and battery limits.

skills.name: Integrate a task executive with language commands
skills.description: Connect dialogue and LLM tool calls to robot skills through a task executive that checks mode, preconditions and safety limits before each action.

skills.name: Integrate legs in place of the wheeled base
skills.description: Replace the wheeled base with a leg module, update the hip interface, mass properties and models, and test on a gantry with fall protection.

skills.name: Manage falls of a bipedal humanoid
skills.description: Plan fall protection with gantries and tethers, detect imminent falls, command a protective falling posture and inspect for damage after any fall.

skills.name: Milestone I06: integrate and verify a humanoid upper body
skills.description: Integrate torso, two arms with hands and an expressive head, then verify coordinated bimanual and head motion against requirements with test reports and an updated FMEA.

skills.name: Milestone I07: integrate a wheeled humanoid that navigates and manipulates
skills.description: Integrate the upper body on a wheeled base that navigates among people and performs pick-and-place tasks, verified by repeat-run tests within power and stability limits.

skills.name: Milestone I08: verify a conversational protocol droid that performs tasks safely
skills.description: Verify a droid that converses, takes spoken requests, performs tasks through guarded tool calls and passes risk assessment, safety validation, privacy review and user acceptance.

skills.name: Milestone I09 (optional): integrate bipedal locomotion into the humanoid
skills.description: Integrate legs into the verified protocol droid so it walks on a physical biped platform, with fall safety, updated risk assessment and repeat-run walking trials.
